papers.title: Long-term results of the modified Dunn procedure in slipped capital femoral epiphysis
papers.abstract: Aims In situ fixation for slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) prevents further displacement, but fails to correct the proximal femoral deformity, which may lead to femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and early osteoarthritis (OA). The modified Dunn procedure (MDP) restores proximal femoral anatomy with the aim of improving long-term joint preservation. However, evidence beyond mid-term follow-up remains limited. This study evaluates the ten-year survivorship, functional outcomes, and radiological correction following MDP. Methods A retrospective single-centre review was performed of patients treated with the MDP between 2007 and 2014 for stable or unstable SCFE of any severity. Patients with preoperative avascular necrosis (AVN) were excluded. Primary outcomes were ten-year survivorship free from conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) and from radiological OA progression (≥ 1 Tönnis grade). Secondary outcomes included patient-reported outcome measures, hip range of motion, clinical signs of FAI, and correction of the Southwick and α angles. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed and stratified by slip severity. Results A total of 35 hips (34 patients) completed ≥ ten years of follow-up (163 months (SD 34)). Ten-year THA conversion-free survivorship was 88.6%, decreasing from 100% in mild slips to 86.4% in moderate and 83.3% in severe slips. Ten-year OA progression–free survivorship was 82.9%, with rates of 100%, 81.8%, and 66.7% for mild, moderate, and severe slips, respectively. The mean ten-year functional scores were high (modified Harris Hip Score 88.9 (SD 4.4); University of California, Los Angeles Activity Scale 8.9 (SD 1.6); and Merle d’Aubigné-Postel 17.7 (SD 0.9)). Substantial radiological correction was observed, with the Southwick angle improving from 45.0° to 13.1° and the α angle from 85.8° to 50.9°. No postoperative AVN occurred. Conclusion At ten-year follow-up, the MDP achieved excellent functional outcomes and effective deformity correction in SCFE, with high survivorship in mild and moderate slips. However, progression of hip OA was less favourable in severe slips. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(10):1295–1303.

papers.title: High performance white blood cell classification using ensemble CNNs with Monte Carlo dropout and conformal prediction for clinical uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Automated classification of white blood cell (WBC) images may support cell-morphology workflows, but high accuracy alone does not establish clinical readiness. We developed an Uncertainty-Guided Deep Ensemble (UGDE) combining MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B0, and ShuffleNetV2 with Monte Carlo dropout, temperature scaling, split conformal prediction, and Grad-CAM. The primary dataset contained 16,027 single-cell images from 78 patients (33 with leukemia and 45 without leukemia). All stated development partitions were grouped by patient, and augmentation was restricted to the proper training subset. On the held-out internal test set (3,205 images from 16 patients), UGDE achieved approximately 99% image-level accuracy and macro-F1 of 0.99. Expected calibration error was 2.3% before and 0.8% after temperature scaling. Internal empirical conformal coverage was 94.2%, 89.7%, and 79.7% at nominal coverage levels of 95%, 90%, and 80%, respectively; these slight shortfalls are reported without claiming that the targets were met. External evaluation used 2000 Raabin-WBC images after mapping the nine model outputs to five shared leukocyte categories and yielded 94% descriptive accuracy. Grad-CAM examples were used as post-hoc visualizations and were not interpreted as causal explanations. These retrospective results support further evaluation of uncertainty-aware WBC image classification, but they do not demonstrate performance on whole slides, automated differential counts, prospective patients, or clinical workflows.

papers.title: Non-linear mechanical field reconstruction coupling recurrent neural networks with physics-informed graph neural networks
papers.abstract: Reconstructing local stress fields in heterogeneous microstructures under non-linear, history-dependent loading remains a major computational bottleneck in multi-scale simulations. We propose a coupled LSTM-GNN framework that links the temporal and spatial aspects of local stress field reconstruction. A Long Short-Term Memory network encodes macroscopic stress–strain sequences into a compact hidden state that captures the path-dependent constitutive response, while a physics-informed Graph Neural Network reconstructs the spatially-resolved stress field at each time step. We introduce a relative weighting strategy with linear warm-up to balance the data-driven reconstruction loss and a discrete divergence-based equilibrium penalty. This resolves the scale mismatch that prevents fixed-weight formulations from converging in the elasto-plastic regime. The model is trained on 10,000 non-proportional loading paths applied to a periodic plate-with-a-hole microstructure and von Mises elasto-plasticity. The model achieves three orders of magnitude speedup over finite element simulations and generalizes to loading sequences twice the training length, with 3.0% cumulative error. Because the graph relies on mesh connectivity instead of the specific element type, one trained surrogate can be applied directly without retraining to meshes with different element types and to both coarser and finer resolutions, while in all cases reproducing the high-fidelity quad-element FE field used during training. Indeed, the message passing characteristics inherent to GNN and MeshGraphNet architecture render the model mesh-agnostic. Analysis of the LSTM hidden states suggests a low-dimensional structure related to the internal state variables of the constitutive model.

Personalized in situ bioprinting of skin: designing a blueprint for clinical translation
papers.abstract: In situ 3D skin bioprinting offers a revolutionary paradigm for directly regenerating massive cutaneous defects right on a patient’s wound bed. However, translating this technology from the bench to the bedside remains heavily bottlenecked by hostile wound microenvironments, delicate cell viability constraints, and unpredictable tissue deformation during surgery. To overcome these primary hurdles hindering its clinical translation, this review proposes a comprehensive blueprint for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into the in situ bioprinting of skin. It describes how AI can optimize bioinks, design patient-specific grafts from medical images, and enable real-time adaptive printing through predictive modeling and feedback. The review presents a framework for developing intelligent, portable systems for personalized skin therapy while addressing biomaterials, personalization, quality control, and AI-related ethical issues. This roadmap ultimately bridges the gap between delicate laboratory protocols and autonomous, precision-guided intraoperative interventions tailored for real-world clinical deployment.

papers.title: Design, characterization and in vitro evaluation of biomimetic hierarchical scaffolds with TPMS‑gyroid structure for bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Abstract Human physical and mental health are significantly impacted by maxillofacial alveolar bone defects. The emergence of additive manufacturing metamaterial scaffolds provides a new treatment strategy for this. Due to the complexity of the jawbone and the difficulty in preparing bionic hierarchical gradient scaffolds, most current research focuses on human long bones. This study first proposes a metamaterial scaffold that simulates the jawbone. The stratified scaffolds (G300-600, G300-750,G300-900) adopt the Gyroid structure of the triply periodic minimum surfaces (TPMS), with the upper and lower layers respectively simulating the cortical bone and cancellous bone of the jawbone. And a large-aperture uniform scaffold (G750) was designed as a control. And it is prepared through digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology. The results show that sintering the scaffold to 1170℃ and holding it for 48 hours can improve the mechanical properties and biocompatibility of the scaffold, making it match. G300-600 not only improves in vitro neovascularization and new bone formation, but also features a high level of compressive strength (9.86MPa) and outstanding degradability. This gradient metamaterial scaffold has a structure, mechanical properties and biological activity that conform to the jawbone, providing a new strategy for bone defects in the maxillofacial region.

papers.title: Robotic‐Arm Assisted Direct Anterior Approach Total Hip Arthroplasty Facilitates Tensor Fasciae Latae Preservation and Early Functional Recovery in Obese Patients
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of robotic‐arm assisted (RA) direct anterior approach (DAA) total hip arthroplasty (THA) in facilitating tensor fasciae latae (TFL) preservation and subsequent functional recovery, and to explore the correlation between TFL preservation and postoperative inflammation, pain, and early functional recovery in obese patients. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 69 obese patients (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ) undergoing primary DAA‐THA from September 2023 to December 2024 with 12‐month follow‐up. Surgical procedures were performed by RA technology in 31 patients (RA group) and manual technology in 38 patients (M group). Demographic characteristics, perioperative parameters, TFL injury index, unsupported ambulation duration, creatine kinase (CK), C‐reactive protein (CRP), Visual Analog Scale scores (VASs), Harris Hip Scores (HHS), Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), Forgotten Joint Score‐12 (FJS‐12), radiologic measurements, and complications were retrieved from patients. Student's t ‐test and Mann–Whitney U test were used to compare continuous data. Fisher test and Chi‐square test were used to compare the categorical data. Longitudinal data were evaluated by generalized estimating equations. The relationships between TFL injury index and early clinical outcomes were evaluated using Spearman's correlation analysis. Results Baseline demographic characteristics of both groups were comparable. RA group demonstrated significantly lower TFL injury index (18.05 [IQR 14.51–30.05] % vs. 38.31 [IQR 20.58–50.70] %, p = 0.001) and shorter unsupported ambulation duration (3.00 [IQR 2.00–4.00] week vs. 5.00 [IQR 3.00–6.00] week, p < 0.001) compared to M group. Besides, TFL injury index showed a strong positive correlation with unsupported ambulation duration ( ρ = 0.775) ( p < 0.001). Compared to M group, RA group significantly reduced CK, CRP, and VASs at the initial 72 h postoperatively (all p < 0.05). RA group exhibited significantly superior HHS, WOMAC, and FJS‐12 compared to M group at postoperative 1 month (all p < 0.01). TFL injury index demonstrated strong positive correlations with CK ( ρ = 0.619), CRP ( ρ = 0.628), and VASs ( ρ = 0.652) at postoperative 72 h (all p < 0.001). Furthermore, it showed a strong negative correlation with HHS ( ρ = −0.615) and FJS‐12 ( ρ = −0.759), and moderate positive correlations with WOMAC‐pain ( ρ = 0.410) and WOMAC‐function ( ρ = 0.583) at postoperative 1 month (all p < 0.001). Despite longer operative duration in RA group, it exhibited a significantly higher proportion of acetabular components positioned within the Lewinnek safe zone and a significantly lower incidence of incision‐related adverse events compared to M group (all p < 0.05). Conclusion In obese patients undergoing DAA‐THA, RA technology significantly reduced intraoperative injury to TFL. This muscle preservation effect was significantly associated with attenuated early postoperative inflammation, lower pain levels, and faster functional recovery.

papers.title: Biomechanical comparison of stand-alone interbody bone grafting versus cage implantation in ULIF: a finite element analysis
papers.abstract: The biomechanical differences between stand-alone interbody bone grafting and cage implantation in unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar interbody fusion (ULIF) remain unclear. This study compared the two strategies in a patient-specific finite element model and assessed model credibility using geometric reconstruction, published range-of-motion (ROM) data, and mesh convergence analysis. A subject-specific L4-L5 finite element model with residual Grade I spondylolisthesis was used to compare bilateral pedicle-screw fixation with stand-alone interbody impaction bone grafting versus porous titanium cage implantation. A 500-N axial preload and a 7.5-N m pure moment were applied independently in six directions. Segmental ROM, model-reported stiffness, and von Mises stresses in the interbody constructs, screw-rod system, and endplates were evaluated. ROM was calculated from the relative rotation of L4 with respect to L5. In addition to comparison with published cadaveric ROM, five characteristic mesh sizes (4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.5, and 2.0 mm) were assessed under identical model settings. Cage implantation reduced ROM by 30.4%-37.3% across the six loading directions and produced higher model-reported stiffness than stand-alone bone grafting. The cage model also generated higher localized stresses in the interbody construct and screw-rod system; during right lateral bending, screw and rod stresses increased by 556.6% and 361.2%, respectively. Endplate effects were direction- and level-dependent, including a 326.7% increase at the L4 inferior endplate during right lateral bending. In the mesh study, the monitored von Mises stresses for 4.0-, 3.5-, 3.0-, 2.5-, and 2.0-mm meshes were 6.820, 11.499, 9.849, 9.865, and 9.840 MPa, respectively; the maximum pairwise difference among meshes of 3.0 mm or finer was 0.25%. Within the prescribed loading, material, contact, and mesh assumptions of this single patient-specific model, cage implantation provided greater immediate segmental restraint but generated a less favorable localized stress environment in selected implant and endplate regions. Stand-alone bone grafting produced greater motion but a more diffuse load-transfer pattern. The mesh convergence results support numerical stability of the reported stress solution but do not constitute independent biological validation. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as proof of clinical superiority, long-term safety, or a direct basis for patient selection.

papers.title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
papers.abstract: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting.

papers.title: Machine learning-accelerated sustainable inverse design of ultra-wideband THz metamaterial absorber
papers.abstract: Terahertz absorbers are progressively relevant to sustainable energy and sensing where material and computational efficiency are essential. We demonstrated a six-layer IGIGIM (Insulator–Graphene–Insulator–Graphene–Insulator–Metal) metamaterial absorber that achieves >90% absorption across 12.95 THz (6.07–19.02 THz), peaking at 99.99% near 11.85 THz. The structure maintains its performance up to 60° for both polarizations, demonstrating good tolerance to incidence-angle variations. Rather than relying on full-wave simulations, we developed a machine learning surrogate trained on FDTD (Finite-Difference Time-Domain) data to accelerate design exploration. Bayesian optimization identified high-performing designs using ∼60% fewer simulations than random search. Multi-objective analysis further revealed viable trade-offs among bandwidth, total thickness below 30μm, and angular robustness, supporting compact designs with reduced computational and material requirements. SHAP analysis showed that incidence angle dominates performance variation. Uncertainty quantification further allowed us to flag low-confidence predictions for selective FDTD validation, creating a reliability-aware workflow while reducing unnecessary computational effort.

papers.title: A hybrid deep Kronecker and BN-eLU-AlexNet framework for early prediction of learner outcomes in e-learning platforms
papers.abstract: Introduction Early prediction of learner outcomes in online learning environments can support timely academic intervention and learner support. Methods This study proposes DKBNE-AlexNet, a hybrid architecture combining a Deep Kronecker Network branch, a feature-token batch-normalized eLU AlexNet-inspired branch, gated residual fusion, and a wide linear residual path. Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, 24,153 enrolments from 22 module presentations and 22,234 learners were analyzed. Eighty-four predictors were constructed from learner characteristics, course design, and engagement during the first 25% of each presentation. The target was the weighted mean of tutor-marked and computer-marked assessment scores. Models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation grouped by module presentation and repeated three times. Results DKBNE-AlexNet achieved an MAE of 11.424 (95% group-bootstrap CI 10.389-12.560), RMSE of 14.843, and R 2 of 0.117. Random Forest and LightGBM achieved slightly lower MAEs of 10.916 and 10.918, respectively, but the presentation-level difference between DKBNE-AlexNet and Random Forest was not statistically significant (Wilcoxon p = 0.388; Holm-adjusted p = 1.000). Distinct learning materials accessed and active learning days were among the strongest predictive contributors. Discussion DKBNE-AlexNet provides a competitive and stable framework for early learner-outcome prediction, while strong tree-based models remain important baselines. The framework is best interpreted as an early-warning learning-analytics tool rather than a direct measure of teacher effectiveness.

papers.title: An elasto-viscoplastic fast fourier transform framework for predicting spatially resolved fatigue performance in additively manufactured metals
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of fatigue life in additively manufactured (AM) metals remains challenging due to inherent microstructural sensitivity and corresponding scatter in fatigue performance, particularly under high-cycle fatigue conditions. In this work, a structure-property framework based on crystal plasticity fast Fourier transform (FFT) methods is extended to simulate microstructure-sensitive fatigue-damage evolution; the results of which are used to map location-specific fatigue performance in AM build domains. Cyclic plasticity behavior is captured through the incorporation of kinematic backstress hardening, and fatigue indicator parameters (FIPs) are computed to resolve local propensity for fatigue damage under cyclic loading. The framework is demonstrated on direct energy deposition (DED) stainless steel (SS) 316L microstructures. A FIP-to-life curve is established for the DED SS316L material to map the FIP evolution behavior from simulation to an estimate of lifetime as a function of strain amplitude. A comprehensive convergence study is carried out to quantify the error in estimated fatigue life as a function of the number of explicitly simulated cycles (up to 3000), and the results confirm that reliable fatigue life estimates can be obtained with a limited number of simulated loading cycles under the assumed FIP-to-life approach. Application of the framework across multiple process-informed AM build domains captures spatial variations in fatigue life and reproduces the expected increase in microstructure-induced scatter with decreasing strain amplitude. Furthermore, the computational efficiency of the FFT solver enables high-throughput simulations to support statistical analysis and uncertainty quantification. The proposed framework offers a pathway for integrating microstructure-sensitive fatigue life prediction into fatigue-critical qualification and design of AM components.

papers.title: Multi-material 3D printing by laser powder bed fusion: a review
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to review multi-material three-dimensional (3D) printing by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process. Advancements in the LPBF process for multi-material 3D printing of different metallic alloys, focusing on material pre-alloying and chamber refilling approaches to achieve functionally graded and multi-layered compositions, have been presented. Design/methodology/approach The methodology involved an in-depth analysis of prominent research and peer-reviewed publications related to multi-material 3D printing using LPBF. A database of the Web of Science from the previous 20 years was examined using VOSviewer software for bibliometric analysis to identify research gaps. A networking diagram highlighting the research gap was generated using the study’s obtained relevance score. A case study was conducted for a single-hopper-based LPBF process for multi-material 3D printing of metals, exploring two novel approaches: material pre-alloying and chamber refilling to control material composition and layering with a single hopper. Findings A comprehensive review of multi-material 3D printing by LPBF, followed by a case study, highlights the challenges and advances in single-hopper-based LPBF for multi-material 3D printing of metallic components, focusing on innovative methods (material pre-alloying and chamber refill) to enable compositional gradients and layered structures. A functionally graded material (FGM) comprising 17–4 precipitate-hardened (PH) stainless steel (SS) and Ni625 was successfully 3D printed using chamber refill and material pre-alloying in a single-hopper LPBF system. However, a few limitations apply to multi-material 3D printing using LPBF, including managing phase evolution, mechanical characteristics and material compatibility. Integrating machine learning and AI-driven process optimization can enhance predictive capabilities and facilitate compelling exploration of process parameters to achieve desired material performance and structural integrity. Originality/value This study provided a comprehensive review of multi-material 3D printing using the LPBF technique and discussed a novel single-hopper multi-material 3D printing approach as a case study. This review offers insights into the maintenance and operation of single-hopper LPBF machines as an operational resource for industry/ academia for multi-material printing.

papers.title: Quasi-static compression performance of multiphase 3D-printed PLA–PETG interpenetrating TPMS structures
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattices are attractive cellular architectures owing to their smooth, curvature-continuous geometry, high surface-to-volume ratio, and efficient load-bearing behavior. TPMS structures are widely investigated for lightweight and energy-absorption applications, including impact-resistant protection systems and medical scaffolds. In this work, dual-nozzle fused deposition modeling (FDM) is employed to fabricate single-phase TPMS specimens from polylactic acid (PLA), while a complementary phase structure (CPS) is fabricated from polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG). The combination of these phases results in an interpenetrating phase composite (IPC). Four sheet-based TPMS topologies, namely Primitive, Gyroid, Diamond, and I-graph-wrapped package (IWP), are investigated. Quasi-static compression experiments are conducted to characterize and compare the compressive performance of the interpenetrating architectures and their constituent-phase counterparts. The results demonstrate that IPC architectures outperform the TPMS and CPS phases, revealing a strong synergistic effect induced by phase interpenetration. This structural synergy promotes more uniform deformation and mitigates strain localization. The IWP, Gyroid, and Primitive topologies exhibit the greatest improvements in stiffness, whereas the Primitive and Gyroid architectures achieve the highest yield stress and energy absorption capacity.

SMOTE extensions for abnormal minority instances in imbalanced time series classification
papers.abstract: Abstract Class imbalance remains a significant challenge in time series classification, especially when the minority samples include abnormal or outlier instances. This study proposes four extensions of the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE): Distance Extended SMOTE, Dirichlet Extended SMOTE, Feature-Correlation and Random-Perturbation SMOTE, and Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (BGMM) SMOTE. These methods use weighted neighbor selection, probabilistic modeling, and clustering to generate synthetic samples. Augmentation was applied only to the training data after train–test splitting and within the validation process, while the test data remained unseen. The proposed methods were integrated with a Bayesian Deep Bidirectional LSTM classifier using Monte Carlo dropout-based variational inference to enable both robust classification and uncertainty quantification. Experiments on five benchmark time-series datasets showed that based on stratified 10-fold cross-validation, the proposed SMOTE extensions consistently surpassed baseline methods and standard SMOTE. BGMM-SMOTE and Dirichlet Extended SMOTE achieved the best performance. The present study gives a detailed analysis of SMOTE enhancements specifically designed for abnormal class distributions, providing an appropriate method to handle imbalanced time series classification. The framework combines advanced resampling methods with Bayesian deep learning to make more reliable predictions, with applications in healthcare monitoring, fault detection, and other safety-critical fields.

papers.title: A Dual-Medium Model-Based Method for Rapid Thermal Performance Analysis of TPMS Porous Heat Exchange Structures
papers.abstract: The triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure demonstrates significant potential in the field of active heat transfer. This is due to its high specific surface area and controllable pore connectivity. However, its intricate geometric features result in notable computational costs during RANS-based CFD simulation, greatly limiting the efficiency of its design and optimization processes. Although existing equivalent approaches (e.g., the volume averaging method and the porous media model) have reduced the computational burden to some extent, they still suffer from limitations. Theseinclude insufficient sensitivity to microstructural features and low accuracy in characterizing convective heat transfer. In order to address the temperature-field prediction biases caused by the above limitations when filling TPMS on a large scale, this paper proposes a rapid analytical method based on a dual-medium model. The core idea of this method is to idealize the TPMS structure as a continuous solid thermal conductive medium and to homogenize its internal flow channels into a coexistent Darcy–Forchheimer fluid medium. The thermal conductivity tensor of the equivalent solid is accurately calculated via the homogenization method, whereas convective heat transfer in the fluid medium is characterized using empirical correlation equations. Ultimately, a rapid analytical model coupling solid heat conduction and fluid convection is developed at the macroscopic scale. Numerical examples show that, compared with traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods, this method improves computational efficiency by approximately 22 times while retaining high accuracy, thus providing an effective tool for the rapid design and performance assessment of TPMS-based active heat transfer structures.

papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning Combined with Feature Selection and Bayesian Optimization for Predicting Rare Earth Elements and Yttrium in Coal: A Case Study of China’s Five Major Coal-Bearing Regions
papers.abstract: Abstract Determining the concentrations of rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) in coal is essential for evaluating coal-hosted critical metal resources and understanding their geochemical controls. However, conventional laboratory analyses are costly, time-consuming, and spatially sparse, limiting regional-scale assessment. In this study, we compiled 527 coal samples from 30 coalfields across China’s five major coal-bearing regions and developed an explainable machine learning framework for REY prediction. Unlike previous site-specific models, this framework integrates feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and SHAP interpretation for REY prediction at a broad regional scale. After data preprocessing, multicollinearity diagnosis, and correlation-based feature selection, 16 predictors were retained for model construction. Four ensemble regression models, including Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees (ET), CatBoost (CAT), and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), were optimized using Bayesian hyperparameter search and 5-fold cross-validation. The ET model achieved the best test-set performance among the four ensemble models, with RMSE = 39.962, MAE = 29.669, and R2 = 0.716, although predictions for highly enriched samples remained uncertain because of the long-tailed REY distribution. SHAP analysis identified Ga as the most influential predictor, followed by geological age and P2O5, suggesting that clay-related terrigenous input, stratigraphic context, and minor phosphate-associated phases may jointly influence model-predicted REY enrichment. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can serve as an effective prescreening tool to prioritize coal samples for detailed REY analysis, while independent validation is recommended for high-value target areas.

papers.title: Hydraulic variability as the governing parameter in hidden hydropower assessment: A standardised framework for water infrastructures
papers.abstract: Water infrastructures host a largely unexploited hidden hydropower potential that could power distributed monitoring systems without external supply. However, its assessment remains challenging due to the lack of standardised, transferable evaluation procedures. This work develops a unified framework for hidden hydropower assessment, integrating multi-year operational velocity data with a physics-informed, neural-network-accelerated reduced-order model and an energy-based optimisation procedure that maximises annual harvested energy under realistic flow variability. The framework is validated across eighteen pilot sites spanning pressurised pipe networks, small open-channel systems and large open-channel environments. The cross-site analysis reveals two novel scientific findings. First, a statistically robust inverse relationship exists between the coefficient of variation of flow velocity (CV) and the capacity factor across all infrastructure categories ( R 2 = 0.8408 ), establishing CV as one of the dominant drivers of long-term energy utilisation that cannot be inferred from device-level, steady-flow studies. Second, the optimal design velocity may deviate from both the mean and the most frequent velocity, owing to the cubic scaling of extractable power with flow speed, confirming that variability-aware optimisation is physically necessary, not merely preferable. Together, these findings support a quantitative site suitability map classifying candidate locations as Suitable, Marginal or Unsuitable based solely on operational flow data, without requiring preliminary harvester sizing. Sites with CV < 0.1 and medium-to-high velocities achieve capacity factors above 80%, suitable for direct sensor powering, whereas sites with CV > 0.2 show severely limited utilisation regardless of instantaneous velocity.

papers.title: A Physics‐Informed Machine Learning Model for Predicting Fatigue Delamination Growth With Fiber Bridging‐Defined Confidence Intervals in Composite Laminates
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In fatigue delamination growth (FDG), for different fiber bridging intensity and load ratios ( R ‐ratios), the Paris‐type law on FDG rate ( da/dN ) is formulated using strain energy release rate ( SERR ) on the crack tip Δ√ G tip and effective SERR Δ√ G eff as similitude parameters. The resulting da/dN (Δ√ G tip ) and da/dN (Δ√ G eff ) data collapse into a band. Based on this finding, this paper proposes a physics‐informed machine learning (PIML) framework to characterize the FDG scatter. The framework is composed of three PIML models. PIML 1, with integrated modified beam theory (MBT), predicts the SERR . PIML 2‐a and 2‐b, with the modified Paris relation and using Δ√ G tip and Δ√ G eff as similitude parameters, predict the da/dN and its 95% confidence intervals under a single or multiple R ‐ratios using the SERR s from PIML 1. Bayesian optimization is adopted to optimize hyperparameters for PIML 1 and 2‐a/b. The developed PIML framework can be utilized for variability‐enabled prediction in composite laminates.

papers.title: Knowledge Construction and Co-Construction in the Era of Team-Based Care: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Knowledge construction and co-construction are central to preparing health professions students for collaborative, team-based care. However, evidence on how these processes are conceptualised, supported, and studied in health professions education remains dispersed. Methods This scoping review was conducted in accordance with JBI guidance for scoping reviews and reported using the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Arksey and O’Malley’s framework informed the stages of identifying the research question, searching for relevant studies, selecting studies, charting data, and collating and summarising findings. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and PsycINFO were searched for peer-reviewed empirical studies published before June 2025. After duplicate removal, 2,311 records were screened, 274 full texts were assessed, and 20 studies were included. Results Studies covered medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students. Key facilitators included structured collaborative modalities, active learning strategies, and technological tools. Challenges comprised time constraints, unequal student participation, technical barriers, limited digital literacy, and divergent clinical reasoning perspectives. Conclusions Knowledge construction and co-construction in health professions education are supported by intentional pedagogical, technological, and relational scaffolding. Future research should more clearly operationalise these constructs, examine interprofessional contexts, and develop strategies to address participation imbalances, time pressures, and inequitable access to learning opportunities.

papers.title: OP‐Follower: Onboard Vision‐Based Obstacle‐Aware Predictive Person Following for Quadruped Robots via IBVS‐NMPC Control
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents OP‐Follower , a fully onboard, pure vision‐based, obstacle‐aware person‐following framework for quadruped robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on LiDAR, infrastructure, or offboard computation, OP‐Follower operates exclusively on visual inputs and runs entirely on a Unitree Go2. OP‐Follower bridges the gap between low‐frequency, computation delay‐prone visual perception and safety‐aware high‐rate control by integrating YOLO‐World–based open‐vocabulary person detection, BoxMOT multi‐object tracking, and Kalman filter–based delay‐aware prediction within a unified planning–control architecture that tightly couples image‐based visual servoing with nonlinear model predictive control. A decoupled artificial potential field–based visual obstacle avoidance strategy is further employed to ensure collision‐aware navigation without interfering with target tracking objectives. Comprehensive evaluations in high‐fidelity Gazebo simulations and real‐world indoor and outdoor environments, including long‐distance following, dynamic pursuit–evasion interactions, and multi‐person scenarios, demonstrate robust real‐time performance with fully onboard processing at a 50 Hz control rate. Compared with a non‐predictive baseline, OP‐Follower reduces pixel‐space and distance tracking errors by up to 57.2% and 50.5%, achieving representative root‐mean‐square errors of approximately 13–16 pixels and 0.09–0.11 m under sharp turning motions, while maintaining stable outdoor performance, including a continuous 1.4 km trial. GitHub page with demo videos is available at https://op-follower.github.io/ .

papers.title: AI-Driven Hull Defect Evolution Prediction: A Hybrid Physics-Informed Deep Learning Framework for Maritime Structural Health Monitoring
papers.abstract: Ship hulls operate under repeated wave impact, changing loading conditions, and prolonged exposure to seawater. Over years of service, these effects can produce corrosion, local pitting, and fatigue cracks in important structural members. In practice, hull condition is still assessed largely through scheduled drydock surveys and empirical wastage relationships. Such inspections are valuable, but they provide only limited information about what happens between two survey periods. This paper develops a hybrid deep-learning approach that combines a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) with a SpatioTemporal Graph Neural Network (ST-GNN) to estimate the future development of hull defects. Instead of relying only on measured inspection data, the model also uses corrosion behavior and Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics as physical constraints during training. Measurements from different nondestructive testing sources, including ultrasonic gauging and autonomous underwater vehicle observations, are brought into a common structural representation. The evaluation described in this work uses 15 years of inspection data from 142 compartments of a Post-Panamax bulk carrier. Over a five-year prediction period, the reported corrosion-wastage MAE is 0.089 mm, while the RMSE for fatigue-crack propagation is 0.94 mm. The reported results show a 71.4% improvement over the recurrent baseline considered in the study. The physical constraints also prevent unrealistic outcomes such as an increase in plate thickness without repair or a negative crack-growth rate. The resulting workflow can be used as a computational aid for condition-based maintenance and continuous hull assessment.

Explicit Spin Regulation as an Emerging Design Paradigm in Heterogeneous Catalysis
papers.abstract: Conspectus Catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability arise from coupled electronic, structural, interfacial, transport, and spin-related processes. Conventional catalyst design has relied largely on electronic effects, strain or stress engineering, active-site construction, and local reaction environment control. Although these strategies have enabled major advances, they do not fully capture the spin degrees of freedom associated with open-shell transition-metal centers and magnetically responsive catalysts. Spin state, spin polarization, magnetic moment, spin density, and magnetic ordering can influence adsorbate binding, transition-state stabilization, charge transfer, and reaction pathways, yet their catalytic consequences are often grouped under the broad label of magnetic enhancement without a clear mechanistic assignment. In this Account, we develop explicit spin regulation as a framework for magnetism-informed catalysis. Magnetic enhancement describes an observed response to a magnetic field, a magnetic component, or a magnetic environment. Explicit spin regulation, by contrast, requires deliberate modulation of spin-related variables at or near catalytically active sites and a mechanistic connection to catalytic function. We organize this framework around two routes. Catalyst-integrated spin levers use promoters, interfaces, or interphases to tune the active-site spin/electronic structure, whereas field-induced spin levers introduce external fields or catalyst-localized magnetic perturbations during catalysis. Although implemented differently, both routes seek to control how the active-site spin governs adsorption, transition-state energetics, charge transfer, selectivity, stability, and durability. Our studies provide representative evidence for this framework. Promoter-induced spin modulation stabilizes the N–N dissociation transition state beyond conventional electrostatic promotion, establishing the spin-promotion effect as a catalyst-integrated design principle. In electrocatalysis, external fields, embedded nanomagnets, and magnetic proximity effects provide progressively localized perturbations that can be connected to spin-sensitive active sites, key intermediates, or local magnetic ordering. These examples also show why performance enhancement alone is insufficient. A convincing assignment should connect the imposed perturbation, the active-site spin/electronic response, the affected intermediate or transition state, and the resulting catalytic consequence. Magnetic measurements, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, element-specific X-ray spectroscopies, operando methods, kinetic analysis, and spin-polarized theory provide complementary elements of this evidence loop. Building on this mechanistic framework, we further translate the active-site spin into catalyst-design descriptors. The local metal-center spin moment can be correlated with oxygen-intermediate adsorption and activity trends, enabling descriptor-guided screening of dual-atom catalysts. Spin-related variables may also inform stability and durability through their connections to phase stability, surface reconstruction, active-site preservation, dissolution resistance, and long-term operation. Generalizing these insights requires paired, standardized, and machine-readable datasets that connect magnetic perturbations, active-site structures, spin-sensitive measurements, catalytic metrics, and durability under comparable conditions. Artificial intelligence-assisted literature mining, knowledge graph construction, high-throughput spin-polarized calculations, active learning, and magnetism-aware machine-learning interatomic potentials may help identify transferable spin descriptors and extend spin-regulated catalyst design to dynamic interfaces. The broader aim is to move magnetism-informed catalysis from phenomenological enhancement toward predictive control through deliberate regulation of the active-site spin.

papers.title: Consensus Collision‐Free Trajectory Planning for Multi‐AUV Formation Gathering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Formation gathering of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is a fundamental prerequisite for cooperative underwater missions. It enables AUVs initially located at dispersed positions to form a prescribed geometric configuration before formation‐based exploration, observation, or survey tasks. Each AUV must reach its assigned terminal position and heading while ensuring coordinated motion and inter‐vehicle safety. Trajectory planning must simultaneously account for inter‐AUV collision avoidance, vehicle kinematic constraints, motion feasibility, and limited underwater acoustic communication. This paper proposes a consensus‐based distributed trajectory planning method for multi‐AUV formation gathering by integrating finite‐control‐set model predictive control (FCS‐MPC) with optimal reciprocal collision avoidance (ORCA) constraints. Before trajectory execution, common initial mission information is obtained through polling‐based acoustic broadcasting. Based on this shared information, each AUV independently generates a consistent gathering trajectory set without requiring continuous inter‐vehicle communication. The terminal pose of each AUV is determined from the target pose of the leader AUV and the prescribed formation geometry. A staged guidance strategy is introduced to improve convergence through position approach and terminal heading regulation. Meanwhile, ORCA‐based velocity‐space constraints are incorporated into the FCS‐MPC framework to generate collision‐free and feasible motion subject to constraints on surge speed, yaw rate, and minimum turning radius. The proposed method was evaluated through randomized simulations and lake trials. In 50 randomized simulation runs involving six AUVs, formation gathering was successfully completed in all runs without inter‐AUV collisions. The minimum inter‐AUV distance was 26.82 m. The maximum terminal position and heading errors were 0.954 m and , respectively, and the average planning time was 2.662 s. In lake trials involving three Wukong 1000 AUVs, UHF radio was used to emulate polling‐based acoustic broadcasting for initial mission‐information synchronization. The AUVs then executed the independently planned trajectories. The average tracking error of each AUV was below 1 m, while the terminal position and heading errors remained within the prescribed tolerances of 10 m and , respectively. These results demonstrate the safety, feasibility, and implementation potential of the proposed method for multi‐AUV formation gathering without continuous inter‐AUV communication.

papers.title: Thermal management and fast charging optimization for lithium-ion battery energy storage systems: A data-driven nonlinear model predictive control approach
papers.abstract: Fast charging capability is critical for maximizing energy throughput and operational flexibility in lithium-ion battery energy storage systems. This paper proposes a data-driven thermal management strategy combining Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) modeling with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC). Using LUT-based variable-current charging data acquired from physical battery-pack tests across eight ambient temperatures from 17°C to 40°C, ridge regression identifies thermal dynamics at discrete temperature breakpoints, forming an LPV model that adapts to varying conditions. The model is embedded in NMPC framework to optimize charging current via rolling-horizon optimization under representative-temperature, current, and current-rate constraints. Under purged rolling-origin validation on unseen continuous time/SOC windows, the Ridge-LPV model achieved an R2 of 0.9331 and an RMSE of 0.991 m°C for one-step temperature-increment prediction relative to the recorded representative battery-temperature signal. Closed-loop controller performance was evaluated through MATLAB R2022a/Simulink simulations. Under matched paired operating conditions, the proposed strategy reduced charging time by at least 6.97% relative to the LUT baseline while maintaining the specified 50°C representative-temperature constraint. The proposed approach provides a computationally efficient and interpretable solution for NMPC-oriented fast-charging studies in battery energy storage systems.

papers.title: Parrot Mambo Minidrone as a benchmark platform for low-cost UAV research: a review of control, autonomy, software validation, safety and experimental evaluation
papers.abstract: Low-cost minidrone platforms are increasingly used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) research for safe indoor experimentation, controller development and engineering education. The Parrot Mambo Minidrone is particularly attractive because of its compact size, onboard sensing, MATLAB/Simulink compatibility and suitability for real-time validation. This review critically synthesises 137 studies published between 2018 and 2026 involving the Parrot Mambo, including studies where it appears alongside other UAV platforms. The literature spans modelling, state estimation, classical and intelligent control, robust nonlinear control, disturbance rejection, vision-based navigation, multi-UAV coordination, Human-Drone Interaction (HDI), software validation, cyber-resilience, education, safety analysis, energy-aware evaluation and hardware performance. A platform-centred taxonomy is developed to trace progression from Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID)-based stabilisation toward adaptive, intelligent, perception-driven, software-aware and safety-conscious autonomy. PID and Proportional-Integral–Proportional-Derivative (PI-PD) controllers remain important baselines, while fuzzy-PID, Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Model Predictive Control (MPC), Model-Free Control (MFC), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Observer-Based Control (OBC) and Fault-Tolerant Control (FTC) address nonlinearities, disturbances, uncertainty and hardware constraints. However, software testing, cyber-resilience, fault diagnosis, reachability analysis, actuator health, aerodynamic constraints and energy-aware evaluation remain weakly integrated. The principal gap is the absence of a standardised benchmark jointly assessing control accuracy, robustness, perception reliability, energy use, computational load, software dependability, cyber-resilience, safety, actuator constraints and real-flight repeatability. Accordingly, this review proposes a benchmark-driven framework for integrated, safety-aware, hardware-aware and reproducible Parrot Mambo research.

papers.title: An efficiency-oriented physics-informed transfer learning framework for transient simulation across diverse properties and conditions in liquid energy pipelines
papers.abstract: As pipeline-transported liquid energy has expanded to include hydrogen-based and bio-based fuels, achieving efficient and rapid simulations across diverse physical properties and conditions is essential for timely early warning of anomalies. However, conventional numerical computation is hindered by iterative parameter identification, precluding computational efficiency. Emerging physics-informed machine learning techniques necessitate excessive retraining whenever fluid properties or conditions change, which might take hours. Furthermore, they struggle to accurately capture the transient oscillatory characteristics induced by coupled trends of flowrate and pressure. To address these challenges, this study proposes an efficiency-oriented physics-informed transfer learning framework for accelerated transient simulation under diverse properties and conditions. First, a Trend-Aware Gating Physics-Informed Neural Network (TAG-PINN) is designed to characterize the trend synchrony and divergence of transient hydraulics by incorporating a trend-gating layer to quantify the dependency strength between flowrate and pressure. Subsequently, a Similarity and Physics-driven Transfer (SPT) learning framework is developed, which quantifies similarities between domain samples to achieve high-fidelity simulation while minimizing the data overhead. Moreover, the contribution of network layers is quantified to enable the selection of high-contribution layers for a cost-effective, high-precision adaptation. Pragmatic experiments demonstrate that TAG-PINN captures transient oscillations more accurately, significantly reducing flowrate and pressure simulation errors by 58% and 51%, respectively, over conventional PINNs. The proposed SPT framework reduces training time by one to two orders of magnitude, bringing fine-tuning time from the hour scale to the minute scale, thereby providing effective technical support for timely early warning and decision-making in industrial pipelines.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Adopting the “glycan language” framework, we survey how AI addresses each, emphasizing the systems on which it has been tested. In synthesis planning, GlycoPredictor uncovered anomeric-selectivity rules such as the anti-nitrile and C2-azido α-directing effects, while Bayesian optimization discovered lithium-salt-directed stereoselective glycosylation; for site identification, ESM-2 with AlphaFold2-derived structural features improves N- and O-glycosite prediction, and DeepGlycanSite maps carbohydrate-binding interfaces. For structure and dynamics, AlphaFold3 and multimodal cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, and molecular dynamics (MD) modeling move glycoproteins toward conformational ensembles, as in the AI-assisted dissection of the MCTS1–JAK2–IFN-γ axis. In glycomics, deep learning resolves intact glycopeptides and de novo glycan topology and has defined Fc N-glycan signatures of immunoglobulin G in autoimmune and malignant disease. Because glycan language models link sequence and structure to function, they are becoming clinically actionable: they prioritize candidate variants in congenital disorders of glycosylation and stratify immune disorders and tumors by aberrant glycosylation. Remaining obstacles include scarce structure-linked datasets, encoding of branched topologies, multimodal fusion, and interpretability.

papers.title: Generative AI-Supported Learning, Cognitive Offloading, and Metacognitive Awareness: Examining Changes in Students’ Learning Regulation
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships among generative AI-supported learning, cognitive offloading, metacognitive awareness, and students’ learning regulation among university students in Pakistan. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was employed, and data were collected from 293 university students through a self-administered online questionnaire distributed using Google Forms. The collected data were organized in Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographic characteristics, Pearson correlation was applied to examine relationships between variables, and simple linear regression was conducted to assess predictive relationships. The illustrative analysis indicated a positive association between generative AI-supported learning and metacognitive awareness (β = 0.478, p = .001), with the regression model explaining 22.8% of the variance in metacognitive awareness (R² = 0.228). Cognitive offloading was positively associated with students’ learning regulation (r = 0.436, p = .001), while metacognitive awareness positively predicted learning regulation (β = 0.568, p = .001), explaining 32.3% of its variance (R² = 0.323). These findings highlight the potential relevance of generative AI use and metacognitive awareness to students’ learning regulation. The study emphasizes that AI tools should support, rather than replace, independent thinking, critical evaluation, and active learning. Educators may use these insights to design learning activities that promote reflection, self-monitoring, and responsible AI use. The study also provides a basis for future research examining these relationships across different academic disciplines and educational settings. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretations and does not establish changes in learning regulation over time.

papers.title: An Intelligent Integration Layer for Physics–AI Collaboration in Digital Drilling: Architecture, Interface Contracts, and Numerical Demonstration
papers.abstract: Drilling systems generate abundant predictions from sensors, physics-based models, digital twins, and artificial intelligence (AI), yet the step from prediction to engineering decision remains fragmented across modules and human expertise, and no established framework specifies how uncertain, heterogeneous predictions should be combined and checked against hard limits before an action is taken. This research article proposes, specifies, and numerically demonstrates an Intelligent Integration Layer (IIL) between model outputs and control execution. The gap is diagnosed as three interface defects: heterogeneous uncertainty that is not fused, uncertainty truncated to point estimates at module boundaries, and hard limits that are softened into penalties or checked only against nominal predictions. The IIL addresses these through three stages (Engineering Understanding, Reasoning, and Decision), explicit interface contracts, and a reproducible reasoning procedure in which candidate actions are generated around the current operating point, eliminated by a joint chance constraint, ranked, and assigned a confidence score that gates decision authority. In a synthetic drilling-ahead study, the strongest supported result is that a sample-based joint chance constraint reduced realized constraint violations from 24.6% of reasoning cycles under hard constraints on mean predictions to 1.4%. Confidence gating reduced them further, to 0.7%, but did so largely by referring 65% of cycles to a conservative simulated engineer, and its confidence score did not distinguish reliable from unreliable admissible recommendations; the gated policies are therefore reported as exploratory counterfactuals, and a policy that implements the confidence-authority rule in this reduced simulation, with engineer confirmation as the highest authority, is reported alongside them. The principal contributions are a diagnosis of the prediction-to-decision gap as a set of interface defects rather than model deficiencies; a specification of the integration layer, comprising interface contracts, a reproducible reasoning procedure, and gated levels of decision authority, whose contracts make the dimensions and time dependence of engineering feasibility explicit; and a positioning of that layer relative to chance-constrained optimization, model predictive control, safety filters, and deployed intelligent drilling systems, which clarifies what the IIL adds and what it inherits.

papers.title: Thermal characteristic analysis and optimization research of new energy vehicle battery thermal management system based on numerical simulation
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the issues of excessive temperature rise, uneven temperature distribution, and increased cooling energy consumption in new energy vehicle power batteries under high-rate charging and discharging and complex operating conditions, this paper proposes a multi-physics coupled modeling and optimization method for battery thermal management systems based on numerical simulation. First, an electro-thermal-fluid coupling framework is established, including SOC estimation, an electrical model, a Bernardi heating model, an equivalent thermal network, and a fluid-structure interaction heat transfer model, to describe the battery’s heat generation, solid-state heat conduction, and convective heat transfer processes of the cooling medium. Second, temperature, velocity, and pressure field analyses are conducted for both air-cooled and liquid-cooled structures to reveal the influence mechanisms of flow channel structure, flow distribution, and local heat transfer capacity on battery thermal uniformity. Based on this, nonlinear model predictive control and the NSGA-II multi-objective optimization method are introduced, with the highest temperature, maximum temperature difference, and cooling energy consumption as optimization objectives, to obtain a Pareto compromise solution between thermal safety and energy consumption. Finally, the effectiveness of the model is verified by comparing experimental temperature data with the model prediction results. The results show that the proposed method can effectively capture the battery’s thermal response characteristics and provides a theoretical basis for the structural design and operational optimization of power battery thermal management systems. The numerical results demonstrate a 6.7% reduction in maximum battery temperature and a 15.3% reduction in cooling energy consumption after optimization. The reduced-order model achieves an R2 of 0.987 with an RMSE of 0.38 K and provides an 18.0× computational speed-up compared with the full-order model, while experimental validation achieves an R2 of 0.986 with an RMSE of 0.41 K. The NSGA-II optimization converges at approximately 150 generations with a final hypervolume of 0.965, confirming the effectiveness and computational efficiency of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Composite Model Predictive Control Strategy for Triple-Active-Bridge-Based MMDTC-PET with Enhanced Disturbance Resilience
papers.abstract: To address the delayed dynamic response and susceptibility to overcurrent surges of the triple-active-bridge (TAB)-based modular multilevel DC-link T-type converter power electronic transformer (MMDTC-PET) under load step transients, this paper proposes a composite model predictive control (MPC) strategy to enhance the system’s disturbance rejection capability. The proposed strategy adopts a hierarchical control architecture comprising a proportional-integral (PI) outer power loop and an MPC inner loop. To tackle the heavy computational burden caused by multi-port coupling, dimensionality reduction is performed by equating the phase-shift ratios of the two primary-side ports of the TAB, which effectively mitigates the computational cost. Furthermore, a dynamic overcurrent hard-constraint penalty term and a control-effort smoothing term are incorporated into the multi-objective cost function. This not only achieves steady-state error-free tracking of the output voltage but also enhances physical operational safety under complex conditions at the algorithmic level. Comparative simulation results under various operating conditions demonstrate that, compared with the traditional PI-based phase-shift control, the proposed strategy exhibits a faster dynamic response under load step conditions. Moreover, it suppresses transient power overshoots and overcurrent impacts during input voltage sags and recoveries, thereby significantly improving the transient disturbance rejection capability and operational robustness of the system.

Machine Learning Prediction for Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Direct C-3 Arylation of Imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines
papers.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed direct C-3 arylation of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines has witnessed significant advances in recent years. However, identifying optimal reaction conditions for this transformation relies heavily on labor-intensive trial-and-error experiments, which consume significant time and costs. To address this challenge, 275 valid reaction data entries conforming to the reaction mechanism were collected as training data, including substrates, catalysts, additives, solvents, reaction temperature, and experimental yield. Three mainstream tree-based ensemble regression models, including GradientBoosting, Random Forest and ExtraTrees, were constructed after strict data cleaning and advanced feature engineering for systematic benchmark comparison. The GradientBoosting model, which delivered the best fitting and generalization performance among all candidates, was selected as the objective function for subsequent constrained Bayesian optimization. A constrained Bayesian optimization algorithm (with predicted yield bounded within 0–100%) was adopted to globally screen high-dimensional reaction parameters for maximum yield. Comprehensive cross-model evaluation indicated the test-set determination coefficients followed the order GradientBoosting (R2 = 0.4416) > Random Forest (R2 = 0.3864) > ExtraTrees (R2 = 0.3544), while the root mean square error (RMSE) of GradientBoosting was 15.3144, outperforming the other two models in prediction stability. Under the optimal parameter set recommended by GradientBoosting (catalyst Pd(acac)2BuAd2P, reactants ref-5-1d and ref-9-2d, additive CsOAc, solvent DMA, 150 °C), the model predicted a theoretical maximum yield of 100%, whereas Random Forest and ExtraTrees only reached predicted peak yields of 83.63% and 80.80%, respectively. This multi-model benchmarking workflow eliminates the bias risk from single-model prediction, provides an efficient tool for optimizing metal-catalyzed C-3 arylation of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines, and can be generalized to other complex transition-metal catalytic systems.

papers.title: Development of New Al-Ca-Cu-Mn-Zr Alloys for Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: The limited thermal stability of conventional aluminium alloys at elevated temperatures restricts their application in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). In this study, a novel Al6Ca3Cu1.8Mn0.4Zr (wt.%) alloy was developed for improved thermal stability via stable intermetallic phases. LPBF processing of gas-atomised powder identified a reference processing window at 350 W and a hatch distance of 0.08 mm (~97–122 J·mm−3), enabling fabrication of crack-free samples with relative densities above 99.0%. The as-built microstructure consists of a highly refined cellular structure with a quasi-continuous network of intermetallic phases and nanoscale dispersoids within the α-Al matrix, resulting in a yield strength of 206 ± 15 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 312 ± 2 MPa and an elongation of 2.7 ± 0.2%. Annealing (350 °C/3 h) leads to partial fragmentation and spheroidization of intermetallic phases, accompanied by a slight decrease in strength (UTS = 277 ± 10 MPa) and elongation (2.4 ± 0.3%), while fracture remains predominantly ductile. The alloy shows softening resistance: room-temperature hardness remains close to the as-built value after annealing at 250–300 °C, whereas more pronounced softening is observed after annealing at 350–400 °C, with subsequent stabilization during prolonged holding.

papers.title: Generative AI-Supported Learning, Cognitive Offloading, and Metacognitive Awareness: Examining Changes in Students’ Learning Regulation
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships among generative AI-supported learning, cognitive offloading, metacognitive awareness, and students’ learning regulation among university students in Pakistan. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was employed, and data were collected from 293 university students through a self-administered online questionnaire distributed using Google Forms. The collected data were organized in Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographic characteristics, Pearson correlation was applied to examine relationships between variables, and simple linear regression was conducted to assess predictive relationships. The illustrative analysis indicated a positive association between generative AI-supported learning and metacognitive awareness (β = 0.478, p = .001), with the regression model explaining 22.8% of the variance in metacognitive awareness (R² = 0.228). Cognitive offloading was positively associated with students’ learning regulation (r = 0.436, p = .001), while metacognitive awareness positively predicted learning regulation (β = 0.568, p = .001), explaining 32.3% of its variance (R² = 0.323). These findings highlight the potential relevance of generative AI use and metacognitive awareness to students’ learning regulation. The study emphasizes that AI tools should support, rather than replace, independent thinking, critical evaluation, and active learning. Educators may use these insights to design learning activities that promote reflection, self-monitoring, and responsible AI use. The study also provides a basis for future research examining these relationships across different academic disciplines and educational settings. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretations and does not establish changes in learning regulation over time.

A Cyber Risk Quantification and Governance Architecture for Critical Infrastructure: From Posture Measurement to Executive Reporting
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity governance in critical infrastructure organizations requires defensible, decisiongrade quantification of risk that withstands board, investor, and regulatory scrutiny. Traditional heat map approaches conflate likelihood and impact estimation with subjective judgment in ways that resist comparison across business units, programs, and years. Cyber risk quantification methods address these limitations by translating control posture, threat intelligence, and asset impact into monetary loss distributions and prioritized investment decisions. This paper presents a cyber risk quantification and governance architecture tailored to critical infrastructure organizations. The architecture spans five domains. The posture measurement domain captures control maturity and operational evidence from information technology, operational technology, and third party sources. The exposure analysis domain identifies the most material attack paths through asset modeling and adversary informed scenarios. The loss modeling domain uses methods consistent with the Factor Analysis of Information Risk standard and related approaches to translate exposure into monetary distributions. The portfolio analysis domain integrates loss estimates across business units, presenting risk concentration, treatment options, and trade offs. The executive and regulatory reporting domain communicates results to boards, investors, and regulators with appropriate uncertainty quantification. The architecture aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology cybersecurity framework, the National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800 30 on risk assessment, the International Organization for Standardization 31000 risk management guidelines, and emerging Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure expectations. The paper illustrates the architecture through three scenarios in energy and water infrastructure and closes with implementation guidance, governance considerations, and an agenda for future research. papers.title: Art Analysis in Occupational Therapy Education: Building Foundational Skills and Reflective Awareness of Implicit Bias
papers.abstract: Occupational therapy education requires instructional approaches that help students move beyond memorizing foundational concepts to applying them in meaningful ways. This instructional insight describes the integration of structured art analysis into a first-semester Occupational Competence course as an experiential strategy for teaching the Occupational Therapy Practice Framework (OTPF-4) and activity analysis. Through individual, classroom, and museum-based learning experiences, students engaged in guided observation, discussion, reflection, and application using artwork as a low-risk context for developing observational and interpretive skills. Evidence of student learning included confidence surveys and written reflections completed throughout the instructional sequence. Students reported increased confidence in applying OTPF concepts and activity analysis, while reflections demonstrated greater awareness of how personal experiences and implicit bias can influence interpretation. Students also described the importance of considering multiple perspectives and avoiding premature assumptions before drawing conclusions. By intentionally connecting art analysis to occupational therapy practice, this instructional approach helped students apply foundational occupational therapy concepts while fostering reflective awareness that supports thoughtful professional judgment. Structured art analysis offers occupational therapy educators an engaging and adaptable strategy for promoting active learning and preparing students to apply foundational knowledge in future clinical practice.

papers.title: Metallurgical Aspects of Additively Manufactured Aluminum Alloys: A Review
papers.abstract: The Additive Manufacturing (AM) of aluminum alloys, especially via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), offers exceptional potential for producing lightweight, high-strength components with tailored geometries. However, the rapid solidification and repeated thermal cycling inherent to LPBF-based AM often result in undesirable features such as porosity, anisotropy, residual stress, and solidification cracks, especially in high-strength alloys such as the 2XXX, 6 XXX, and 7 XXX series. This review critically examines the metallurgical landscape of aluminum alloys processed via LPBF, beginning with a comparative overview of conventional series (2XXX-8 XXX) and highlighting their printability and processing limitations. It then explores the influence of processing parameters and alloying additions on grain refinement, including the role of inoculants like TiB2, LaB, and Al3(Sc,Zr) in promoting equiaxed microstructures. Among these, VED is a critical processing parameter with an optimized range (typically 50–150 J/mm3), enabling fine grain structures, high densification, and6 superior mechanical performance. Phase stability was evaluated in terms of precipitation behavior, transformation kinetics, and defect formation under LPBF-specific conditions. Post-processing techniques, such as T6 Heat Treatment (HT) and hot isostatic pressing (HIP), have been shown to significantly improve mechanical performance by mitigating microstructural heterogeneity and enhancing the strength–ductility balance. Finally, the review outlines emerging trends such as data-driven alloy design and nanoparticle-assisted solidification control. By correlating process–structure–property relationships and synthesizing insights across microstructure, mechanical behavior, and process design, this study outlines a strategic roadmap for optimizing AM (LPBF) aluminum alloys to enable reliable, high-performance applications at the industrial scale. papers.title: Frequency Stability Assessment and Synthetic Inertia in Low-Inertia Power Systems: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources (RESs), particularly solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power, has significantly reduced the rotational inertia traditionally provided by synchronous generators, creating unprecedented challenges for frequency stability in modern power systems. Reduced system inertia results in higher rates of change of frequency (RoCoF), deeper frequency nadirs, and increased vulnerability to disturbances, necessitating advanced frequency assessment and synthetic inertia solutions. This paper presents a comprehensive review of frequency stability assessment methods and synthetic inertia techniques for low-inertia power systems. First, the fundamental principles of frequency dynamics, inertial response, and the impact of renewable energy penetration on system inertia are discussed. Subsequently, recent advances in deterministic and probabilistic frequency stability assessment methodologies are reviewed, followed by a critical evaluation of virtual synchronous machines, droop-based virtual inertia, model predictive control, battery energy storage systems, grid-forming converters, and intelligent control strategies for synthetic inertia provision. A comparative analysis of existing studies highlights their methodologies, performance metrics, advantages, and practical limitations. The review further identifies key research challenges, including uncertainty modeling, adaptive inertia allocation, converter operational constraints, computational complexity, and real-time implementation. Finally, future research directions toward uncertainty-aware frequency assessment, adaptive synthetic inertia, artificial intelligence-assisted control, and resilient converter-dominated power systems are discussed. This review provides a comprehensive reference for researchers and power system engineers developing reliable frequency stability enhancement strategies for future renewable-dominated electricity networks.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Power System Frequency Regulation Supported by Wind and Energy Storage Systems: State-of-the-Art Methods
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power in modern low-inertia power systems, frequency regulation (FR) faces significant challenges, primarily due to rapid frequency dynamics and stochastic power fluctuations. Energy storage systems (ESSs) can provide fast-responding bidirectional power support as well as virtual inertia, playing a critical role in enhancing system frequency stability. However, existing reviews provide limited systematic analysis linking model fidelity and operating constraints to the reported performance and applicability of wind–storage FR strategies. To address this gap, this paper reviews state-of-the-art FR strategies involving wind power and energy storage systems and provides a comprehensive analysis of key approaches, including optimization-based methods such as model predictive control (MPC) for multi-area systems and distributed MPC, as well as data-driven and intelligent techniques, such as deep reinforcement learning and soft-computing-based controllers. The comparison connects modeling assumptions and operating constraints with frequency response and energy-related evaluation metrics to clarify the benefits, limitations, and applicable conditions of different strategies. Finally, future research directions are proposed. This review offers a systematic reference for the analysis, design, selection, and evaluation of wind power and energy storage FR strategies in modern power systems.
