papers.title: Coupling dynamics of topological states in an acoustic glide-dislocation lattice
papers.abstract: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupling dynamics between two topological states in an acoustic glide-dislocation lattice. By mapping the lattice structure to a two-waveguide model based on coupled-mode theory, we establish a quantitative link between macroscopic coupling behaviors and microscopic geometric parameters. Then, we demonstrate topological Bloch oscillation and topological supermode propagation under single-state excitation and eigenstate-matched excitation, respectively. The topological Bloch oscillation exhibits strong robustness against structural perturbations, whereas the topological supermode propagation undergoes moderate amplitude and phase fluctuations under the same perturbations. This work lays a solid foundation for exploiting coupled topological states in acoustic wave manipulation and may inspire future applications in integrated acoustic devices.

papers.title: Formal-Verification-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Non-Intrusive Last-Mile Coverage Closure
papers.abstract: Last-mile functional coverage closure for modern chip designs remains costly because a mature UVM environment exposes many controls while direct hits on the remaining bins are sparse. We present a non-intrusive workflow that closes pre-defined bins in an existing, human-authored functional coverage model; it does not synthesize verification objectives from the design specification. The workflow first uses abstract-syntax-tree (AST) parsing and cone-of-influence (COI) tracing to map each residual target to existing testbench knobs. Under a matched 20-simulation budget, Bayesian optimization (BO) is compared with continued constrained-random verification (CRV) and random search over the same AST/COI-reduced space. Formal reachability then removes only targets supported by complete unreachability proofs, after which retained targets are grouped by formal difficulty and processed by group-specific BO under a second matched 20-simulation budget. Cleanup and grouping never add numerator bins; only simulator coverage artifacts do. On OpenTitan AES, first-pass reduced-space BO reaches 241/271 bins; formal cleanup removes two denominator bins; the integrated post-cleanup stage - difficulty grouping, policy routing, and group-specific BO - adds 20 simulator-confirmed hits, yielding 261/271 raw coverage (96.31%) and 261/269 effective coverage (97.03%). On Entropy Source, first-pass reduced-space BO reaches 2117/2277 bins; formal cleanup removes ten denominator bins; the integrated post-cleanup stage - difficulty grouping, policy routing, and group-specific BO - adds 93 simulator-confirmed hits, yielding 2210/2277 raw coverage (97.06%) and 2210/2267 effective coverage (97.49%). These results characterize the integrated diagnosis-and-search workflow; the present evaluation does not isolate the causal contributions of difficulty classification, policy routing, and post-cleanup BO.

papers.title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. Existing autoregressive approaches often implicitly rely on the generative model itself to retain such information, leading to spatial memory decay beyond the active context. We introduce World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model with a test-time training memory that consolidates past observations into dedicated model parameters. To robustly update this memory, we propose a recursive least-squares rule that incrementally absorbs novel visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Our TTT memory reads out previously observed scene features from the fast-weight state by camera pose, enabling consistent generation with constant storage and per-step computation regardless of rollout length. To facilitate real-time interactive generation with this robust memory, we further distill the autoregressive model into a few-step generator via dual-teacher distribution matching. On a long-horizon revisit benchmark, World-T3 raises revisit PSNR from 13.52 to 18.31 dB and reduces absolute rotation error from 3.344 to 1.075 relative to the strongest baseline on both metrics, while sustaining 20.6 FPS at 1280 x 704 on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.

papers.title: Measure Neural Mappings
papers.abstract: We introduce and define measure neural mappings (MNMs), which combine measure-dependent neural transport with ensemble consistency for learning operators on probability measures. Ensemble consistency requires outputs from growing ensembles sampled from an input law to converge to the specified population output in probability. We establish quantitative continuum limits for attention on noncompact laws under strong sub-Gaussian and tail-integrability assumptions. These laws accommodate unbounded state spaces in scientific machine learning, including Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification. For fixed self-attention transformers, the expected output Wasserstein error is bounded by the empirical input Wasserstein error plus an additional $N^{-1/2}$ attention term. These self-attention transformers are MNMs under the stated assumptions: pre-norm architectures follow from compact stability after normalization, while post-norm architectures are covered under the stated tail conditions. We prove corresponding cross-attention estimates and extend the results to multihead attention and grouped transformer evaluation, with convergence as the group size grows. For Set Transformers viewed as measure-to-vector mappings, we obtain an $N^{-1/2}$ bound on the expected Euclidean output error under the stated assumptions. Experiments on seven operators in dimensions $d=1,2,3,5,10$ support the predicted particle-count dependence, using one-dimensional Wasserstein computations and Sinkhorn approximations in higher dimensions. The observed Wasserstein and sliced Wasserstein decay rates are close to their respective theoretical sampling benchmarks.

papers.title: Global Extendability of Flat Cliques in Sparse Moment Relaxations
papers.abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while the moment matrix carries more information than the bound itself. When the moment matrix satisfies the flat truncation condition, the bound is tight and global minimizers can be extracted from the matrix. In correlatively sparse relaxations, it is common that only some blocks are flat. We study whether such partial flatness still reveals part of a global minimizer. On a unicycle trajectory optimization problem, repeatedly extracting the atoms of flat cliques and fixing them recovers feasible, near-optimal trajectories. We then construct a counterexample whose relaxation is tight and has a rank-one flat clique, yet the unique extracted atom cannot be extended to a global minimizer. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for global extendability that involve only the boundary of a clique. Every extracted atom minimizes its clique objective given its boundary value, and when the bound is tight and the boundary moment block has rank at most one, the extracted atom of the clique is globally extendable.

papers.title: HybridDualPathNet: Cross-Fusion Attention of EfficientNetV2 and Swin Transformer for Brain MRI Classification of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Separating Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), and Healthy Controls (HC) using structural MRI remains challenging because disease signatures overlap and model performance can be strongly affected by data partitioning. We present HybridDualPathNet, a hybrid architecture combining EfficientNetV2-S for local features and Swin-Tiny for global context through a Cross-Fusion Attention (CFA) module. We evaluate the model in two experiments. First, on the Kaggle APD-3-Class dataset using an image-level split, the model achieves 98.25% accuracy. Second, on a combined Kaggle and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset containing 17,859 slices, we use a per-source split with patient-wise separation for ADNI subjects. In this setting, the model achieves 73.37% standard accuracy and a macro AUC of 0.880. Source-stratified evaluation reveals a substantial domain gap, with 91.2% accuracy on Kaggle test images and 59.2% on ADNI test images. Temperature scaling reduces expected calibration error from 0.130 to 0.015, while split-conformal prediction achieves 89.5% coverage. Saliency analyses using Grad-CAM++, Integrated Gradients, and occlusion indicate that model activations concentrate on brain tissue. These results highlight the importance of patient-level separation, cross-dataset evaluation, and uncertainty estimation when assessing MRI classification systems. The findings also show that strong performance on a single dataset does not necessarily translate to reliable generalization across imaging cohorts.

papers.title: Multics: Generative Multi-Player World Model with Hierarchical Communication
papers.abstract: Multi-player interactive world models aim to simulate shared environments from multiple players' perspectives, but achieving robust generation while scaling to more players remains challenging. Existing approaches that rely on fully-connected communication (e.g., Solaris) incur quadratic attention costs as the number of players grows, while centralized approaches (e.g., $γ$-World) suffer from interference between unrelated events in a shared global representation. To address these challenges, we present Multics, a multi-player video generation framework with hierarchical communication that structures information exchange across player, group, and global levels. This hierarchy introduces group tokens into self-attention as intermediate group-level representations that aggregate locally relevant player information. These tokens connect to global tokens for cross-group communication, while the hierarchical topology limits direct mixing between unrelated local events. Group-token parameters are shared across group slots, allowing the same communication module to accommodate varying numbers of players without introducing new group-specific parameters. We further propose budget-constrained dynamic grouping based on recent camera trajectories, which adaptively groups relevant players while limiting unnecessary communication. Experiments demonstrate that Multics achieves state-of-the-art performance in 4- and 6-player settings, with improved cross-player consistency, player-specific action and camera controllability, and interference robustness. Moreover, Multics generalizes from 4-player training to 6-, 8-, and 10-player inference without retraining, while reducing self-attention computation compared with fully-connected communication.

Compared with Spatial-Omni on the Sonic-Bench test split, SonicWorld improves direction accuracy from 31.98% to 34.69% and reduces azimuth error from 57.22° to 48.01°. In zero-shot transfer to Spatial LibriSpeech, SonicWorld retains strong localization performance, achieving 73.98% direction accuracy and 19.29° azimuth error, compared with 27.14% and 70.74° for Spatial-Omni.

papers.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control
papers.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) now reason about space well enough to program robots, yet the world models behind robot policies are implicit, held in network weights or predicted video, and cannot be inspected or corrected directly. We present D-World, an explicit world-language-action model built on the Sense, Plan and Act decomposition. A perception agent writes the scene as an executable digital twin using generated vision and geometry code. A planning agent searches for actions in simulation and, after each executed action chunk, revises the twin's object states and named physical parameters against what the robot measured. A parameter revision is accepted only if replaying the latest chunk does not increase any measured residual beyond its tolerance, and every chunk is checked in the updated twin before it runs. Structural mismatches return to perception for reconstruction. We call this measurement-grounded cycle of correction and revision recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which the LLM stays frozen while the world it acts in improves. We model the choice of actions that both advance the task and expose model error as a dual control problem and show that the cost of incorporating evidence into the twin sets the threshold at which probing pays, so cheap local revision counteracts the turn-off of cautious controllers. Each episode runs a real-to-sim-to-real loop, and its recorded twins can be refitted and re-rendered offline into higher-fidelity environments for post-training. Because perception and planning communicate only through the twin and language, either can be replaced by a learned model, and since inference dominates the loop, the loop speeds up with faster models. On a dual-arm robot, towel and toaster tasks show local revisions, such as one reducing the bread's rendered-depth residual from 22.4 to 1.5 mm, that let execution continue without reconstruction.

papers.title: Task-Space Motion-Force Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Precise and Compliant Control under Uncertainties
papers.abstract: In Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC), the control law is implicitly determined by the solution of an Optimal Control Problem (OCP). Consequently, OCP design is often tailored to specific platforms and tasks, demanding extensive expert knowledge and tuning effort. To address this, we propose a unified NMPC framework that directly plans and controls the robot joints subject to task-space motion and force requirements and is capable of seamlessly generalizing across multiple robotic platforms and diverse tasks. Furthermore, optimization-based methods often treat interactions as rigid contacts, making the torque solution sensitive to the modeling errors of the robot dynamics and the environment. We study the intrinsic task-space impedance of our proposed controller, its partial contraction for differential stability and differential passivity under unmodeled interactions. As a result, our framework enables closing the force-feedback loop in the high-level planning layer to achieve precise motion-force tracking performance, addressing the long-standing challenge of force-feedback NMPC. Finally, we validate our framework on physical hardware, demonstrating hybrid motion-force control on a redundant manipulator and compliant locomotion on a quadruped, while preserving core NMPC advantages such as hard constraint satisfaction, optimal redundancy exploitation, and real-time planning under unforeseen interactions.

papers.title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion
papers.abstract: Neural operator splitting composes a library of neural operators, one per physical mechanism, into zero-shot simulators of new equations. We ask whether a pretrained library can instead be adapted and grown from unlabeled trajectories in which multiple mechanisms act simultaneously. We introduce SPLICE, a framework that discovers operators without mechanism labels on mixture data. The contributions of the candidate operators to each trajectory are inferred by solving a convex optimization problem. A calibrated test then assigns each discovered operator the mechanism it implements. Failure cases are also detectable, when the library lacks the required physics or when mechanisms are insufficiently separable. Across one and two dimensional systems, the discovered operators recover mechanisms from unlabeled mixtures and compose into zero-shot simulators of unseen equations; a frozen library can also grow an operator for physics absent from pretraining, without labels and without forgetting. On Navier-Stokes, the discovered operators compose about as accurately as their supervised counterparts.

papers.title: Edge-preserving Bayesian neural networks via hierarchical sparsity-promoting priors
papers.abstract: Recovering piecewise-smooth functions with jump discontinuities from noisy, indirect, and incomplete data is a central task in computational inverse problems. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) with heavy-tailed weight priors have emerged as effective edge-preserving priors for such problems. However, posterior inference for these models remains computationally challenging, and existing approaches settle for point estimates obtained by directly optimizing heavy-tailed log-densities. We propose GSBL-BNNs, which model the neural network parameters hierarchically using sparsity-promoting priors from generalized sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL). The hierarchical formulation recovers several popular marginal priors, including Laplace and Student's $t$ (including Cauchy). A key modeling ingredient, novel among edge-preserving BNNs and native to the hierarchical formulation, couples each neuron's bias to its weights through a shared hyperparameter, so that the induced jump discontinuities are free to occur anywhere in the domain while the conditionally Gaussian structure underlying efficient inference is preserved. Furthermore, we develop a block-coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm for maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. This BCD approach alternates between standard network training with iteratively reweighted $\ell^2$-regularization and exact, closed-form hyperparameter updates for gamma and inverse gamma hyperpriors. Building on the BCD algorithm, we perform approximate Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification (UQ) using deep ensembles. Computational experiments---including signal denoising, deblurring, and inverting a two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation law--- show that GSBL-BNNs deliver accurate, edge-preserving reconstructions with built-in UQ. Compared with Gaussian- and Cauchy-BNNs, they yield more accurate predictive means and avoid overconfident uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
papers.abstract: The penetration-resistant design of concrete structures requires the spatiotemporal evolution of the stress field within the target, whereas in design only the strength grade, the geometry and the projectile parameters are known, and the aggregate arrangement is not. Empirical formulae and scalar-output surrogates serve design screening, and mesoscale finite element models resolve the aggregate-scale response, but one solution cannot cover random aggregate samples at scale, and no framework links mesoscale heterogeneity to field-level prediction. A physics-coupled graph neural operator (PC-GNO) is proposed, which learns in function space the evolution of the mid-plane six-component stress tensor field. The training data are generated by full-scale, aggregate-resolved finite element models and comprise 359 cases at the impact velocities of 100, 135 and 165 m/s, corresponding to compressive strengths of 14, 23 and 48 MPa; the data source is verified by laboratory measurements. The coupling strength of message passing is constructed from the impedance contrast across the material interface, and the update is constrained by spectral normalization. Under the single-step primary setting, the mean accuracy of the three levels is 80.16% (91.45%, 77.80% and 71.22%), i.e. 27.81, 42.46 and 34.16 percentage points above the preceding-frame field of the same window; with 20 664 parameters it exceeds the 87.9% of the best Fourier neural operator configuration (about 812 times as many parameters) and the 71.0% of the closed-form linear regression. The output is the complete six-component tensor field rather than a fixed engineering quantity, so that strength criteria and energy indicators follow from one set of weights. For field-level response prediction in concrete penetration, this result provides a data-driven route, with conditions of applicability defined by the training and the evaluation.

papers.abstract: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

papers.abstract: Keeling et al. [Keeling2026Generative] report on a case study recently conducted by Redgrave LLP in which they assert that Relativity's Generative AI Review tool (aiR) achieved 88% recall while Relativity Assisted Learning (RAL), its machine-learning tool, achieved 64% recall. These results are not comparable because the methods employed have different objectives, because of inter-assessor disagreement, and because they represent different recall-precision and cost-benefit trade-offs. Furthermore, established machine-learning models employing Continuous Active Learning (CAL) show state-of-the-art effectiveness, and superior efficiency, when trained only on a sample of 2,000 first-pass-reviewer responsiveness determinations.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
papers.abstract: Inferring tumor-growth laws from sparse, noisy observations requires more than accurate curve fitting. We study an AI-assisted workflow involving symbolic regression, mathematical admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and large language model (LLM) ranking. Synthetic Gompertz data allow trajectory fit, forecasting, and recovery of the governing growth law to be assessed separately. A dense noiseless control recovers the generating family, but sparse noisy sampling frequently leads to alternative forms. Among retained candidates in the tested configurations, physics-informed neural network refitting often increases growth-law error, whereas classical nonlinear least squares usually reduces it. A separate exploratory analysis of archived LLM rankings shows no consistent improvement over selection by training error and identifies errors in mathematical reasoning. Plausible saturation, accurate trajectory fits, and convincing explanations can therefore coexist with incorrect growth laws. Mathematical validity and law recovery require evaluation alongside predictive performance.

papers.title: Trust-Limited Machine-Learning-Accelerated Nudged Elastic Band Calculations for Small-Polaron Hopping in Rutile TiO2
papers.abstract: Nudged elastic band (NEB) calculations of small-polaron hopping are demanding because nuclear motion is coupled to a self-consistent localized electronic state. Near the charge-transfer region, slow self-consistent-field convergence, localization switching, and competing electronic solutions complicate surrogate-assisted optimization. We develop a Gaussian-process-assisted NEB workflow for this regime and demonstrate electron small-polaron hopping in rutile TiO2 using spin-polarized density functional theory with a Hubbard U correction (DFT+U ) with SIESTA. A joint energy-force Gaussian process (GP) with a Matérn covariance model advances the elastic band, while active-atom root-mean-square and maximum-atom displacement limits constrain surrogate motion relative to evaluated configurations. Reaching these limits triggers first-principles sampling without requiring full surrogate convergence. Three independently DFT-verified 96-atom [001] calculations using 11, 13, and 15 images and different surrogate settings and GP parameterizations yield barriers of 0.1645, 0.1637, and 0.1640 eV, respectively, spanning 0.793 meV. In the 15-image calculation, repeated central-image sampling activates a separately calibrated local GP during surrogate optimization. Final full-band DFT verification gives a maximum projected NEB force of 0.0346 eV/Å. A 324-atom calculation yields a lower barrier of 0.1302 eV, indicating supercell sensitivity and demonstrating feasibility at larger GP observation dimension. The workflow combines controlled surrogate extrapolation, targeted charge-transfer-region interpolation, and independent DFT verification to obtain polaron migration pathways, emphasizing reproducible barriers and full-band force convergence.

papers.title: Relational Learning as World Modeling
papers.abstract: Relational learning typically predicts from a database state, but decision making asks a different question: how will that state change under an action? In operational systems, the answer depends on system-specific dynamics that may not be visible in the database itself. We view each such system as a relational "world" and ask whether a model can infer how it behaves from observed executions. We introduce TabWM (Tabular World Model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM uses them as context to predict the sparse structured edits caused by a new action without parameter updates. Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 rises from 0.016 with no observed executions to 0.685 with 64, where a correct edit must match its operation, relational location, and value. Because these predictions are explicit relational edits, they can be applied recursively to imagine candidate futures and compare actions before they are taken. Broader search over these predicted futures improves the realized return of selected action sequences. Together, these results suggest that relational dynamics can be learned in context, broadening relational learning from modeling system state to modeling how that state changes under action.

papers.title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
papers.abstract: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.

papers.title: Belief Space Planning for Risk Signal Temporal Logic via Mixed-Integer Convex Programming
papers.abstract: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifies robot tasks with spatio-temporal requirements, and its robustness semantics allow planning by trajectory optimization. In practice, robots estimate their state from noisy measurements, and when the information gained from a measurement depends on the state, the robot can actively reduce its uncertainty by planning in the belief space. The resulting problem is, however, generally non-convex, for which gradient-based methods are neither complete nor globally optimal. In this paper, we consider Risk STL (RiSTL) planning in Gaussian belief space and show that an information-form parameterization of the belief, together with a convex relaxation of the belief dynamics, yields a mixed-integer convex program (MICP). We prove that the MICP is sound and complete, and that the relaxation preserves the globally optimal input trajectories. We validate the effectiveness of our method in numerical simulations.

papers.title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
papers.abstract: Accurate modelling of soft tactile sensors remains difficult because finite element methods (FEM) are computa- tionally expensive, while real-time simulators often lack fidelity for hyperelastic deformation. Large physical datasets are also impractical to collect because repeated testing can damage fragile sensors. We present a data-efficient framework that combines limited real-world validation, high-fidelity FEM, and graph neural networks (GNNs) for accurate real-time prediction of two-dimensional tactile deformation in a planar soft tactile structure. The key idea is to decouple validation from training: 82 camera-tracked contact configurations are used only to tune and validate an ANSYS FEM model, which then generates 768 synthetic contact scenarios for GNN training. We evaluate both forward prediction from marker deformation to contact localisation and inverse inference from contact configuration to marker deformation. The validated FEM achieves sub-0.5 mm error in more than 90% of validation cases, while the learned GNN surrogate reaches a mean absolute error of 0.32 mm with millisecond-scale inference, compared with minute-scale FEM simulation. Models trained entirely on synthetic FEM data retain sub-millimetre accuracy on real measurements from the 2D tactile structure, demonstrating strong sim-to-real transfer within the tested planar setting. We further integrate the learned model into a real-time visualisation pipeline, enabling rapid deformation prediction for virtual prototyping and simulator-based design exploration without extensive physical testing.

papers.title: What Limits Cross-Task Generalization in World Action Models?
papers.abstract: Cross-task generalization remains difficult for world action models (WAMs), even when their predicted futures depict plausible manipulation. This gap can be attributed directly: we make this gap directly testable by decoupling a WAM into a world model and an inverse-dynamics model (IDM), then holding the IDM fixed while replacing the source of future images. We introduce Align Once, Evaluate Everywhere (AoE), a camera-space inverse-dynamics model pretrained on large-scale robot data, which provides this recovery interface for different future sources across tasks and environments. Through it, we find that actions recovered from recorded futures of unseen tasks execute almost as well as replayed demonstrations, whereas futures predicted by world models collapse across benchmarks. The failures are not generic: they concentrate on the gripper and interaction geometry while generation capacity is spent on task-irrelevant background. This diagnosis suggests that supervision should target exactly these regions. We therefore introduce the vision-to-action (VITA) loss, which passes generated futures through the frozen AoE and penalizes discrepancies in the recovered actions, redirecting generation toward action-relevant detail. Across two world models and three manipulation benchmarks, this simple change raises the execution success of generated futures from near zero to 47.0%. The same loss also transfers to WAMs and yields consistent gains in native control.

papers.title: DR-APO: Decoupled-Representation Advantage-Guided Policy Optimization from Continuous Control to Embodied Navigation
papers.abstract: Policy representations in reinforcement learning have expanded beyond Gaussian policies to diffusion and flow-matching based generative policies. However, existing RL methods remain representation-specific, lacking a unified optimization interface for emerging generative policies. In particular, extending likelihood-based objectives to multi-step generative policies couples optimization to their internal generation process, where accumulated likelihood ratios can weaken the update signal. Meanwhile, generative-policy-specific methods often rely on multi-candidate generation and critic-based selection, improving overall return while providing limited improvement to the policy itself. We introduce DR-APO (Decoupled-Representation Advantage-Guided Policy Optimization), which decouples policy improvement from policy representation through advantage-guided target improvement and representation-compatible direct action fitting, providing a shared optimization principle for Gaussian, diffusion, and flow policies. Across five MuJoCo-v5 tasks, DR-APO remains competitive with SAC for Gaussian policies and achieves the best aggregate policy-only performance for both diffusion and flow-matching policies. NavDP post-training improves the Success Rate (SR) from 70.33% to 89.55% in simulation and from 25% to 65% in real-world navigation. These results demonstrate a unified policy-improvement principle across Gaussian, diffusion, and flow policies, from continuous-control learning to embodied-policy post-training.

papers.title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments
papers.abstract: Safe robot navigation in unknown, dynamic environments requires more than geometric collision checking: a robot still far from an obstacle may be unable to avoid it because of its speed, orientation, or the obstacle's motion. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis captures this in a value function whose sign separates states that admit a safe continuation from those where collision is unavoidable, but computing it online for every newly observed environment is too expensive. This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on reachability solutions to give optimization-based controllers this information in real time. Since the value function never exceeds the constraint, it equals a directly computed constraint, such as a signed distance, minus a nonnegative dynamics correction. Learning only this correction keeps represented obstacles outside the predicted safe set despite approximation errors. The first two of five methods use the learned function as a terminal constraint in model predictive control, for static local environments and predicted obstacle motion. The next two use it as a barrier candidate in control barrier function safety filters, for static environments and, through pairwise barriers in relative coordinates, for a varying number of moving obstacles. Simulations and hardware experiments on ground and aerial robots show better collision avoidance than geometric and hand-designed baselines, especially for short horizons and moving obstacles. The fifth method replaces the grid-based offline solver, which limits the first four to low-dimensional models. For control-affine dynamics with polytopic inputs, the HJ Hamiltonian is maximized at a vertex, so a parallelizable tree search over vertex inputs can generate training labels. With a loss from the HJ variational inequality, these labels yield barrier candidates for systems with up to 13 states.

papers.title: Towards learning-enhanced solvers for multi-parametric optimization
papers.abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been employed in various ways to accelerate the solution of multi-parametric optimization problems (OPs), which prominently arise in model predictive control (MPC). Early approaches focused on approximating the parametric solution (e.g., the optimal control law) directly by NNs. More recently, learning-based techniques have been used to emulate or enhance solver iterations. For the direct approximation of the parametric solution, it has been demonstrated that exploiting structural properties of the underlying OP facilitates the design of suitable NN architectures. In this paper, we show that structural analysis can also be leveraged to systematically integrate learning into classical optimization algorithms, thereby enhancing their performance.   We formalize our concept for the case of multi-parametric quadratic programs (mpQPs), which frequently arise in linear-quadratic MPC, as a representative application. More precisely, we demonstrate that tailored NNs enable a parameter-dependent fine-tuning of the step sizes in a standard dual projected gradient scheme. The design of the NNs is guided by the observation that optimal step sizes, which permit obtaining the exact optimal solution in finitely many iterations, are piecewise constant functions over the parameter space (e.g., the state space in MPC). We establish key theoretical properties of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in a numerical case study.

Across stages, simulator reliability controls the imagined-data ratio and rollout horizon; within rollouts, chunk-level trust controls replay selection and optimization weight. For recursive imagination without exact grounded continuations, a residual predictor estimates trust without querying future ground truth. On perturbed LIBERO-PRO tasks, MERL reaches 79.7% average success, improves high-threshold learning speed by 10.9% over the matched model-free control, and outperforms same-protocol external baselines across three training seeds. Fixed-data adaptation from 50 demonstrations per task achieves 80.0% average success on two physical-robot tasks.

Our approach uses Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to elicit weights for different interestingness measures based on user preference. We also propose an active learning mode with a sensitivity-based heuristic to minimize user ranking queries while still providing high-quality results. Experiments show that our approach significantly reduces running time and returns precise pattern ranking while being robust to user error, compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

papers.title: XAI-Guided Fourier Domain Generalisation for Pure-Simulation Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has shown strong potential for vision-based autonomous driving, but policies trained in simulation often suffer severe performance degradation when deployed in the real world. Existing sim-to-real methods commonly address this gap through image-transfer-based domain adaptation or policy-agnostic domain randomisation. However, the former requires laborious acquisition of target-domain data and is often limited to the deployment domain, whereas the latter introduces unguided perturbations that may not reflect the underlying sim-to-real discrepancy, leading to suboptimal transfer performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose XFD, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-guided Fourier domain generalisation framework for pure-simulation sim-to-real reinforcement learning. The proposed framework extracts explainability attribution maps from simulated observations, and converts these attributions into policy-conditioned Fourier-domain interventions. By perturbing appearance-sensitive spectral components while preserving task-defining spatial structures, XFD constructs robustness-enhancing visual domains entirely within simulation. Subsequently, the proposed robust policy optimisation guides the policy towards attending to task-critical features while suppressing sensitivity to irrelevant visual information. Extensive experiments in simulation and zero-shot real-world deployment demonstrate that XFD consistently improves traveled distance and reward over standard policy and randomly domain-randomised baseline, especially on unseen maps with cluttered backgrounds. Attribution-based analysis further proves that the proposed policy preserves more consistent task-relevant visual evidence across simulation and real-world observations.

papers.title: Imitation Learning of Avoidance Modes for Efficient Multimodal Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Multimodal model predictive control (MM-MPC) avoids local minima among moving obstacles by solving one optimal control problem (OCP) per combination of avoidance sides, so its computational cost grows exponentially with the number of decision-critical obstacles. We propose SideNet-MPC, which replaces this enumeration with a mode decision learned by imitating MM-MPC as an expert. A graph neural network is trained to predict the expert's minimum-cost mode, one avoidance side per obstacle. Its edges encode, for each obstacle pair, the gap predicted for the moment the vehicle first reaches either obstacle, so a neighbor that blocks a preferred passage can reverse the proposed side. The expert's selection rule compares its minimum-cost mode with the previously executed mode; SideNet-MPC keeps this rule and substitutes the network proposal for the minimum-cost mode. Hence at most two OCPs are solved per control period, and every applied input still comes from an OCP with control barrier function constraints rather than from the network. In $100$ seed-matched closed-loop Monte Carlo runs of mixed traffic, SideNet-MPC reaches $93\%$ of the expert's success rate and needs \SI{18.6}{ms} per control period on a single thread, 48\% less than the expert's \SI{35.5}{ms} on sixteen parallel threads. In a controlled gap sweep, its proposed side reverses in the same gap interval as the expert's, whereas proposers without pairwise edges, trained on the same data, never reverse and all deadlock at the blocked gates of a deterministic scene.

papers.title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
papers.abstract: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.

papers.title: From Simulated Fluids to Living Tissue: Zero-Shot Foundation Model Transfer to Perturbed Embryos
papers.abstract: Morphogenesis is driven by the interplay of genetic regulation and tissue mechanics. In vivo video data is limited, particularly under genetic mutations and environmental perturbations, making generalization beyond the most representative conditions in the dataset challenging. However, at tissue scales, the dynamics of Drosophila can be described as a continuum flow, motivating the usage of representations learned across other physical systems as priors for developmental dynamics.   We investigate finetuning Walrus, a Continuum Dynamics Foundation Model pretrained across a broad set of simulated continuous systems, on tissue velocity fields from only 12 wild-type Drosophila blastoderm videos. We evaluate autoregressive prediction both in-distribution and zero-shot under unseen temperature and genetic perturbations. Zero-shot refers to evaluation on perturbation conditions never seen during wild-type finetuning, without any additional training. In-distribution, a Fourier Neural Operator model trained from scratch achieves best performance on VRMSE. However, Walrus (CRPS) is the strongest model under the most severe distribution shift of unseen samples of mutated embryos and temperature conditions. Interestingly, predictions capture the shape of the mean surface tissue velocity trajectory and its separation between 17°C and 27°C, including the timing of the peak at Germ Band Extension onset, a biologically meaningful milestone of embryo development.   Our results provide preliminary support that representations learned from different dynamical systems can transfer to experimental morphogenesis in developmental regimes, provided they admit a continuum description. More broadly, our results motivate further study of physics foundation models as a new complementary tool for the simulation of morphogenesis in low-data regimes.

papers.title: Exploration strategies for Gaussian process bandit optimization with inference regret guarantees
papers.abstract: Existing cumulative regret guarantees for Bayesian optimization (BO) do not necessarily characterize the quality of the algorithm's final output. This gap is critical under noisy evaluations, where the goal is to return a single high-quality recommendation. To address it, we introduce efficient exploration strategies that can be incorporated into any BO procedure by occasionally replacing the acquisition query with an exploration query. To validate this approach, we bound the Gaussian process posterior standard deviation over the search space via the fill distance of the queries, which measures the largest region left unexplored. We then use this result to derive upper bounds on the inference regret, i.e., the gap between the global optimum and the function value at the algorithm's returned point. Empirically, these exploration strategies improve the final recommendations of existing BO algorithms on synthetic benchmarks, hyperparameter optimization, and a control task.

papers.title: Esports World Model Dataset
papers.abstract: Interactive world models must capture how multiple participants jointly change a shared environment while observing different parts of it. Competitive games make this challenge concrete: players cooperate and compete, while fog of war, team vision and camera placement determine what each can see. Modeling these interactions requires data that connect individual observations and actions to shared state and events. We introduce the Esports World Model Dataset (EWM), a collection of human gameplay spanning StarCraft II, Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2, with 3,053 games and maps and approximately 4,880 player-view hours, including estimated hours for the ongoing CS2 extension. It includes 4,628 completed StarCraft II views, all ten perspectives for 303 Dota 2 matches, and up to ten views per round in CS2. Across these views, replay-clock alignment connects rendered video with game-native actions, structured state and events from the same match. The three games expose complementary observation conditions: private fog of war, shared team vision and first-person viewpoints. In StarCraft II, player-specific entity records further distinguish live observations from remembered snapshots and link co-observed entities across opposing views. Together with temporal alignment, these records allow researchers to distinguish legitimate information differences from disagreement about shared state. By connecting human decisions, shared dynamics and player-specific information, EWM supports research toward jointly controlled multiplayer world models and interactive environments populated by teammates and opponents learned from human play.

papers.title: Backward Conformal Prediction under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: Backward conformal prediction (BCP) fixes the size of a prediction set and estimates its miscoverage, but assumes calibration and test data are exchangeable. We extend BCP to covariate shift through importance weighting, preserving its guarantees when the density ratio is known. We show that BCP's tight miscoverage report depends only on the relative weight assigned to missed calibration examples, explaining why a better domain classifier can sometimes produce a worse estimate. Motivated by the fact that BCP depends only on nonconformity scores, we propose estimating density ratios on sorted score vectors rather than high-dimensional inputs. We prove that this approach recovers the same report asymptotically under an interpretable condition and characterize the resulting bias otherwise. Experiments with simulated and benchmark distribution shifts show that the proposed method improves BCP's miscoverage estimates, while score-based weighting consistently yields more accurate estimates than embedding-based weighting.

papers.title: Autoregressive Decoding as a Martingale: Characterizing the Stochastic Dynamics of LLM Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of language tasks. At their core, autoregressive LLMs are conditional probability models that learn to approximate the next-token distribution given the preceding context. Despite this probabilistic nature, the stochastic dynamics of autoregressive decoding have rarely been investigated from a rigorous probabilistic perspective. In this work, we define the per-step prediction error as the difference between the sampled token indicator and the model's conditional predictive distribution, and prove that the cumulative error process is a martingale with respect to the decoding filtration, implying that its conditional first-order moment is identically zero. Beyond this first-order property, we derive a closed-form expression for the second-order behavior of the martingale sequence: its predictable quadratic variation reduces to $\sum_t\left(1-p(y_t\mid y_{<t})\right)$, computable from realized token probabilities alone. This identity establishes a direct theoretical connection between sequence fluctuations and predictive uncertainty during autoregressive decoding. White-box experiments on Llama-3.x and Qwen2.5 families (1B to 72B parameters) verify that the empirically measured second-order moments closely match the theoretical predictions derived from our martingale analysis. These results provide a probabilistic framework for analyzing autoregressive LLM decoding, reveal intrinsic probabilistic fingerprints of different language models, and establish a rigorous mathematical foundation for LLM-generated text detection and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: CLNO: Conservative Local Neural Operator for Compressible Flow Prediction
papers.abstract: We propose a conservative local neural operator (CLNO) for accurate and generalizable autoregressive prediction of compressible flows. Building upon the locality and translation invariance of the local neural operator (LNO), CLNO introduces a conservative evolution framework based on local subdomains of fixed physical size, separating local mean-state evolution from fine-scale reconstruction. The flow is encoded into subdomain-integrated conservative states and fine-scale features, while a shared local network predicts interface fluxes for finite-volume updates that enforce discrete conservation. A convolutional reconstruction network recovers fine-scale structures using zero-mean basis functions, preserving the updated local means and providing information for subsequent evolution. To accommodate different physical parameters, Reynolds--Mach number conditioning modulates the encoding, flux-prediction, and reconstruction networks, enabling a single model to learn parameter-dependent dynamics and generalize to unseen parameter combinations without retraining. CLNO supports prediction across spatial resolutions, computational domain sizes, and boundary conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved generalization and competitive or higher accuracy compared with LNO, including order-of-magnitude error reductions in representative cases, at approximately three to five times the inference cost on periodic benchmarks. These results demonstrate accurate, generalizable, and physically consistent flow prediction through conservative local evolution and fine-scale reconstruction.

papers.abstract: To improve the surface quality and enlarge the effective polishing region of selective laser melting (SLM) fabricated 316L stainless steel, a laser-assisted magnetorheological polishing (LAMRP) method based on a cylindrical magnetic field array was proposed. Four N52 permanent magnet array configurations were designed and compared by Maxwell simulation. The results indicated that Array IV, featuring an N-S staggered arrangement, achieved the optimal performance with an effective polishing distance of approximately 4 mm. Based on this optimized array, LAMRP experiments were conducted to investigate the effects of laser power and polishing gap on surface roughness (Sa). Laser power showed a non-monotonic influence, with the minimum Sa of 138 nm obtained at 7 W. The lowest Sa of 189 nm was achieved at a polishing gap of 3.0 mm. The optimized magnetic array expands and uniformizes the polishing area, enabling stable nanometric finishing of SLM components.

papers.title: Optimization of reinforced concrete structures using AI
papers.abstract: Optimization of reinforced concrete structures has traditionally relied on mathematical methods to find rational combinations of geometric parameters, material characteristics, and reinforcement while meeting strength, rigidity, and structural suitability requirements. The development of artificial intelligence and machine learning significantly expands the capabilities of this approach. Modern algorithms allow not only to search for optimal design solutions but also to approximate the results of labor-intensive calculations, generate surrogate models, predict structural characteristics, and combine multiple optimality criteria into a single procedure. This research article provides an analytical review of methods for applying artificial intelligence to the optimization of reinforced concrete structures. It examines genetic algorithms, neural networks, machine learning methods, metamodels, hybrid algorithms, and deep reinforcement learning. Particular attention is paid to multi-criteria optimization, computational cost reduction, environmental performance, and the need for regulatory verification of results. The scientific novelty of the article lies in the proposed conceptual model of AI-oriented optimization of reinforced concrete structures, which combines a digital model of the structure, a computational database, a ML surrogate, an intelligent optimizer, and independent finite element and regulatory verification into a single iterative process.

papers.title: Stress Distribution Prediction in front of the crack tip using Artificial Neural Networks: A Data-Driven Approach in Fracture Mechanics
papers.abstract: Understanding the stress distribution in front of the crack tip is essential because this region experiences high stress concentration that can control crack initiation and propagation. This study proposes an artificial neural network (ANN) model as a computationally efficient surrogate model for predicting the stress distribution and stress values in front of the crack tip in a simple cracked geometry. The proposed ANN model complements conventional finite element method (FEM) analyses by enabling rapid stress prediction once the model has been trained. The results show that the ANN model can capture the general relationship between the stress intensity factor, radial distance, angular position, and crack-tip stress. However, its predictive performance strongly depends on the magnitude of the stress intensity factor. At low K values, the ANN model shows significant discrepancies in both stress values and contour visualization, and it cannot accurately reproduce the theoretical butterfly-shaped stress distribution. At higher K values, the predicted stress distribution is closer to the analytical solution, and the contour shape is more consistent. These findings indicate that the present ANN model should be regarded as a proof-of-concept surrogate model with limitations, rather than a replacement for analytical LEFM solutions or FEM analysis.

papers.title: Large Language Model Directed Iteration for the Design of Ultra‐Stable Sodium‐Ion Battery
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into materials discovery is hindered by the trade‐off between exploration breadth and exploitation depth, while the lack of embedded domain knowledge and systematic chemical space compression further limits intelligent materials exploration under data scarcity. Herein, we propose a literature‐knowledge‐directed iterative workflow that combines large language models (LLMs) with Bayesian optimization (BO) for the rational electrolyte design for ultra‐stable sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). LLMs serve as auxiliary tools for knowledge mining, while BO accelerates multi‐objective optimization to obtain electrolyte compositions. The optimized dual‐anion hybrid solvation electrolyte (DHSE) constructs a synergistic solvation structure, which induces the formation of a compact, inorganic‐rich, and mechanically robust cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). The as‐formed CEI layer suppresses parasitic side reactions and accelerates Na + transport by reducing the desolvation barrier. Remarkably, industrial‐scale Ah‐level hard carbon||NaNi 0.3 Mn 0.3 Fe 0.3 O 2 pouch cells assembled with DHSE deliver a high energy density of 107.7 Wh kg −1 , alongside a superior capacity retention of 94% after 100 cycles at 0.5C. This work not only develops a high‐performance electrolyte for practically applicable SIBs but also provides a general human‐agent collaborative framework for intelligent materials development under data‐limited conditions.

papers.title: Adaptive cooperative trajectory tracking control for multi-axle independent steering vehicles considering dynamic load transfer
papers.abstract: Multi-axle independent steering vehicles enable axle-wise steering control, improving trajectory tracking in heavy-duty commercial vehicles. However, dynamic load transfer induces substantial variations in axle-level tire cornering stiffness and lateral-force margins. Consequently, fixed inter-axle steering-angle allocation cannot accommodate differences in lateral control capability, compromising tracking accuracy and vehicle stability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a load-transfer-considered adaptive cooperative trajectory-tracking control strategy. First, a linear parameter-varying (LPV) model characterizes the time-varying vehicle dynamics under load transfer, while an axle-level lateral-force margin index derived from tire friction-circle constraints under varying vertical loads quantifies each axle's relative capability to undertake lateral control tasks. On this basis, a cooperative-game-based adaptive distributed model predictive control framework treats each steering axle as a cooperative decision-making player and coordinates their local objectives through a shared global objective function, enabling vehicle-level cooperative optimization of multi-axle steering. Meanwhile, the twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm learns the nonlinear mapping from vehicle states and axle-level lateral-force margins to relative inter-axle weights, allowing the players' relative weights to adapt to changes in lateral control capability. This mechanism mitigates the adverse effects of load transfer on tracking accuracy and vehicle stability. Controller-in-the-loop simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method improves trajectory-tracking accuracy and overall vehicle stability under dynamic load transfer.

papers.title: Parrot Mambo Minidrone as a benchmark platform for low-cost UAV research: a review of control, autonomy, software validation, safety and experimental evaluation
papers.abstract: Low-cost minidrone platforms are increasingly used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) research for safe indoor experimentation, controller development and engineering education. The Parrot Mambo Minidrone is particularly attractive because of its compact size, onboard sensing, MATLAB/Simulink compatibility and suitability for real-time validation. This review critically synthesises 137 studies published between 2018 and 2026 involving the Parrot Mambo, including studies where it appears alongside other UAV platforms. The literature spans modelling, state estimation, classical and intelligent control, robust nonlinear control, disturbance rejection, vision-based navigation, multi-UAV coordination, Human-Drone Interaction (HDI), software validation, cyber-resilience, education, safety analysis, energy-aware evaluation and hardware performance. A platform-centred taxonomy is developed to trace progression from Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID)-based stabilisation toward adaptive, intelligent, perception-driven, software-aware and safety-conscious autonomy. PID and Proportional-Integral–Proportional-Derivative (PI-PD) controllers remain important baselines, while fuzzy-PID, Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Model Predictive Control (MPC), Model-Free Control (MFC), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Observer-Based Control (OBC) and Fault-Tolerant Control (FTC) address nonlinearities, disturbances, uncertainty and hardware constraints. However, software testing, cyber-resilience, fault diagnosis, reachability analysis, actuator health, aerodynamic constraints and energy-aware evaluation remain weakly integrated. The principal gap is the absence of a standardised benchmark jointly assessing control accuracy, robustness, perception reliability, energy use, computational load, software dependability, cyber-resilience, safety, actuator constraints and real-flight repeatability. Accordingly, this review proposes a benchmark-driven framework for integrated, safety-aware, hardware-aware and reproducible Parrot Mambo research.

papers.abstract: A digital twin (DT) is a computational model that evolves over time to persistently represent the structure, behavior, and context of a unique physical system or process. DTs are characterized by a dynamic and continuous two-way flow of information between the computational model and the physical system. Data streams from the physical system are assimilated into the computational model to reduce uncertainties and improve predictions of the model, which in turn is used as a basis for controlling the physical system, optimizing data acquisition, and providing decision support. The DT paradigm brings along challenging mathematical and statistical questions which were at the center of the workshop.

papers.title: Improved robust trajectory tracking of underactuated AUVs via unified Tube-NMPC with proactive finite-time disturbance compensation in uncertain ocean environments
papers.abstract: This paper presents a unified tube-based nonlinear model predictive control (TNMPC) framework for 3D trajectory tracking of underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) subject to parametric uncertainty and deep-ocean current disturbances. The proposed architecture integrates a nominal nonlinear model predictive planning scheme, tube-based ancillary feedback and a finite-time extended state observer (FTESO) within a single predictive control structure. The FTESO jointly estimates the full system state and lumped disturbances. The state estimate initializes the nominal nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) predictor, while the current disturbance estimate generates a bounded same-cycle feedforward input and the prediction horizon remains nominal. Under the stated sufficient conditions, tube tightening and composite Lyapunov analysis establish an RPI tube, post-entry recursive feasibility and input-to-state practical stability (ISpS). The proposed approach is evaluated on a high-fidelity 6-DOF AUV model through a structured scenario sweep and a continuous Monte Carlo campaign under up to 50% parametric uncertainty and persistent ocean-current disturbances, yielding lower aggregate cross-track, depth and heading errors than the DMPC and TMPC benchmarks on the reported 3D helical and sinusoidal trajectories.

papers.title: Physics-informed artificial intelligence for underground hydrogen storage: A PRISMA-based systematic review of validation, uncertainty, and decision readiness
papers.abstract: Underground hydrogen storage is increasingly positioned as a long-duration flexibility option for renewable-dominated energy systems. Dependable deployment, however, is constrained by coupled uncertainties spanning multiphase flow, pore-scale interfacial physics, reactive transport, and potential microbiological effects. To improve the applicability and generalisability of physics-informed artificial intelligence for underground hydrogen storage, we conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic literature review of studies published from 2020 to 2026. The Scopus and Google Scholar searches retrieved 1071 records. After deduplication, 872 unique records remained, and 676 full texts were assessed for eligibility. From these, 51 primary studies relevant to PI-AI for UHS were retained for synthesis after an evidence-quality appraisal gate, comprising 49 UHS-explicit studies and 2 methodologically adjacent studies, retained for transferable PI-AI insights. We examined the complexity of applying physics-informed learning across pore-to-field scales and how this complexity contributes to barriers to transferability, reproducibility, and decision readiness. Specifically, we synthesised evidence across five themes: pore-scale interfacial physics; reactive transport, sorption, and biogeochemistry; reservoir-scale surrogate architectures; uncertainty and data assimilation readiness; and multi-objective design and operational optimisation. Each study was also coded by task, model family, uncertainty practice, and validation strength. Only 9 of the 51 included studies (17.6%) reported predictive intervals or distributions consistent with quantified predictive uncertainty (UQ-A), and just one of these reported fully calibrated empirical-coverage checks, identifying uncertainty quantification as the most consequential evidence gap in the reviewed corpus.

papers.title: Effect of data leakage on deep learning accuracy for kidney stone classification on CT
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for kidney stone classification on CT frequently report accuracies above 98%, but many are trained on augmented datasets split at the image level, allowing near-duplicate copies of the same slice to appear in both training and test sets. To quantify how much this leakage inflates reported performance, we reassessed a deep learning slice-level classifier under a leakage-free, patient-wise protocol with calibration, uncertainty quantification and cross-center validation, using a multi-center CT dataset of 3,364 original and 35,457 augmented images from 201 patients across three centers. This study proposes no new architecture; its contribution is the quantification and benchmarking of an evaluation effect. Patients were partitioned so that all their images, including augmentations, stayed within a single split, and validation and test sets contained only original images. A hybrid CNN-Transformer classifier was trained alongside matched comparator models on one identical training budget, then retrained under a random image-level split to isolate the effect of leakage, with additional analyses including cross-validation, ten-seed repetition, leave-one-hospital-out testing, temperature scaling, conformal prediction, examination-level aggregation and saliency mapping. Under the patient-wise protocol the classifier achieved an AUC of 0.971, accuracy of 0.962, sensitivity of 0.953, specificity of 0.981 and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.914, with patient-level cluster bootstrap intervals; the leaky image-level split raised accuracy to 0.990 and AUC to 0.999. Across ten seeds the mean inflation was 5.0 accuracy points (95% CI 2.7 to 7.3; paired t test P = 0.0009) and 2.7 AUC points (95% CI 1.4 to 3.9; P = 0.001), present in every seed. A plain ResNet-18 reached a numerically higher AUC than the hybrid model with no significant difference detected, and equivalence was not established; a convolution-free Transformer performed near chance (AUC 0.569). Performance fell on held-out centers. Calibration and selective classification improved reliability, and no sex disparity in sensitivity was found once results were pooled across patients at the patient level. Because the analysis uses eight-bit rendered images without Hounsfield unit information, it is a methodological proof of concept rather than an evaluation of a deployable system. These findings show that image-level splitting substantially overstates real-world performance, and that patient-wise, calibrated evaluation offers a more trustworthy basis for appraisal.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of thermosetting bio-composites by temperature-controlled paste extrusion: application to honeycomb sandwich panels
papers.abstract: Abstract A temperature-controlled paste-extrusion process was developed to enable additive manufacturing of otherwise unprintable thermosetting bio-composites. Bioepoxy was combined with lignin-containing cellulose particles to form a high-viscosity paste. Ambient partial curing raised the apparent viscosity to approximately 10⁵ mPa·s at 1 s⁻¹, after which the premix was cooled to 5–10 °C to retard further crosslinking during loading and deposition. The resulting formulations exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behaviour, were cost-effective, and contained a high bio-based fraction (58–71%). Systematic printability trials demonstrated that direct extrusion of the uncooled paste produced failed specimens, whereas the delayed-deposition route yielded stable, geometrically accurate honeycomb cores. Printed objects displayed good machinability under computer numerical control. As a representative application, hexagonal honeycomb cores were fabricated and bonded between plywood face sheets to produce bio-based sandwich panels. Tensile characterisation of the core material and three-point bending tests of the completed panels confirmed that the printed bio-composite provides adequate stiffness and load-bearing capacity for lightweight structural use. Overall, the process offers a practical route for valorising lignocellulosic fillers in thermosetting matrices and for achieving on-demand solidification in layer-wise fabrication of sustainable cellular structures.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of efficient, durable, and platinum group metal‐free electrocatalysts for alkaline water electrolysis is essential to reduce the cost of green hydrogen. Efficient exploration of the vast possible synthetic space is nevertheless hindered by the slow pace of manual experimentation. Here, a closed‐loop optimization is presented that combines an automated electrocatalyst synthesis and testing system, CatBot, with Bayesian optimization and accelerated stress testing at industrial conditions for the rapid discovery of active and durable NiMo coatings. Distinct regions with exceptionally high activity and stability are identified within limited experimental budgets on a nickel wire substrate, using different search strategies to efficiently navigate the six‐dimensional synthesis space exceeding possible combinations. The most promising coatings are upscaled onto technological nickel foam electrodes showing platinum‐level catalytic activity with overpotentials of 173 mV at –1 in 30 wt.% KOH at for the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the autonomous optimization of functional electrocatalyst coatings under realistic operating conditions.

papers.title: 3D Closed‐Loop Navigation of Magnetic Microswimmers Using Vision‐Derived Depth Feedback
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in autonomous microswimmer navigation, achieving closed‐loop 3D control remains challenging because simple, real‐time depth feedback compatible with standard microscopy is unavailable. This work presents a unified multimodal control framework integrating Model Predictive Control (MPC) with A* path planning for both surface‐bound and free‐swimming locomotion of planar magnetic microswimmers. A propulsion‐only depth regulation strategy uses a signed Fourier‐domain blur metric from a single monocular microscope image to estimate axial position without magnetic gradients or volumetric imaging. This vision‐based method enables real‐time depth estimation and waypoint tracking with minimal computational cost. In experiments, the proposed controller achieved 3D closed‐loop navigation with a median planar error of 12–15 μm and overshoot of 20 ± 5 μm (mean ± SD, n ≥ 20). During fixed‐focus 3D swimming, depth regulation was maintained within an axial working window of approximately 200 μm. papers.title: Bio-inspired electrosurgical knife with lubricant-assisted porous–groove surface and micro-serrated edge for reducing tissue adhesion and thermal injury
papers.abstract: Tissue adhesion and thermal injury remain major challenges in high-frequency electrosurgery because carbonized residues can accumulate on the electrode surface and reduce cutting stability. To address this issue, a coating-free bio-inspired electrosurgical knife was designed and fabricated from 316L stainless steel by selective laser melting. Inspired by loach-skin lubrication and anti-fouling characteristics, a porous–groove blade surface was designed for lubricant storage and transport. Inspired by crab-chela serrations, a micro-serrated cutting edge was introduced to reduce cutting resistance. Fluid-flow simulation showed that the porous–groove surface promoted lubricant retention and local recirculation, reducing near-wall resistance by up to 20.73%. Friction tests indicated that D p = 350 μm and L p = 800 μm produced the lowest lubricated friction coefficient of 0.362 among the tested porous–groove surfaces. Static cutting simulation and cutting-force tests confirmed that the micro-serrated edge reduced cutting resistance, with the lowest peak cutting force of approximately 0.605 N obtained at H 1 = 300 μm. Powered electrosurgical tests showed that the sample with D p = 350 μm, L p = 800 μm, and H 1 = 300 μm achieved the lowest apparent adhesion mass of 2.07 ± 0.67 mg, corresponding to a 61.5% reduction compared with the DT401 commercial smooth control electrode. The thermal damage areas on the upper and lateral tissue surfaces were reduced by 56.75% and 54.44%, respectively. These results demonstrate an effective engineering strategy for improving the anti-adhesion and thermal-safety performance of electrosurgical knives.

papers.title: Mechanisms underlying biomaterial-regulated macrophage polarization in bone tissue engineering: From interface sensing to immune microenvironment remodeling.
papers.abstract: Traditional biomaterials commonly trigger a foreign body reaction after implantation, leading to fibrous encapsulation and poor osseointegration. Advances in osteoimmunology have enabled contemporary tissue engineering to redefine biomaterials as active modulators of the osteoimmune microenvironment rather than as passive scaffolds. At the core of this reconceptualization is the targeted control of macrophage polarization to establish an immune environment conducive to bone repair. The plasticity of macrophages reflects the dynamic balance between the M1 pro-inflammatory and M2 pro-regenerative states; this plasticity ultimately determines regenerative outcomes. This review offers a conceptual four-dimensional regulatory framework that extends from extracellular interface sensing to intracellular genome remodeling and progresses from material properties and signaling cascade stratification to mitochondrial reprogramming and non-coding RNA (ncRNA) networks. Within this framework, material interfaces function as platforms for activating, transducing, and integrating bioactive signals. These signals can be externally modulated to reshape intracellular metabolic organization and sustain mitochondrial function. At a finer regulatory tier, ncRNAs modulate signaling pathways to achieve the precise post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression. Central to this model is a bidirectional, spatiotemporally dynamic feedback loop linking intrinsic cellular machinery with extrinsic material systems. Linking material design parameters to dynamic biological responses lays a conceptual foundation for the development of biomaterials capable of the adaptive and programmable regulation of the osteoimmune microenvironment. Future research may focus on the precise temporal control of M1/M2 phenotypic switching and the coordinated presentation of multiple signals, thereby advancing the development of next-generation immunomodulatory biomaterials for bone repair.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Personalized Insulin Regimens: Integration with Automated Delivery Devices, Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Predictive Algorithms
papers.abstract: Diabetes management, particularly insulin dosing for individuals with type 1 and insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes, remains complex due to variability in glucose levels influenced by diet, physical activity, stress, and illness. Conventional insulin regimens often fail to maintain optimal glycemic control, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), and Automated Insulin Delivery (AID) systems have created new opportunities for personalized insulin therapy. This review highlights the role of AI-driven approaches in optimizing insulin regimens through machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and model predictive control algorithms. These technologies enable real-time adaptive insulin dosing, predictive glucose monitoring, and automated alerts for abnormal glucose fluctuations. Integration of AI with CGM and closed-loop insulin delivery systems has demonstrated improved Time in Range (TIR), reduced HbA1c levels, and lower hypoglycemia incidence compared to conventional therapy. The review also discusses challenges including algorithm transparency, data security, regulatory considerations, and population-specific adaptability. Emerging innovations such as digital twins, federated learning, and fully autonomous closed-loop systems may further advance precision diabetes management and improve patient outcomes.
